articles.title_orig: Park City council weighs China Bridge redevelopment to revitalize Swede Alley corridor
articles.title_zh: Park City council weighs China Bridge redevelopment to revitalize Swede Alley corridor
articles.content_orig:
PARK CITY, Utah — With the southern portion of China Bridge parking garage within a decade of the end of its service life, Park City officials are considering a broader redevelopment of the garage and surrounding Swede Alley corridor. In a discussion during Thursday’s city council meeting, city staff and councilmembers discussed options to pair parking infrastructure with new commercial space, public gathering areas, and improved transportation connections.
Council members weighed whether to follow a relatively straightforward plan to repair and eventually replace the garage or pursue a larger redevelopment of the southern portion of the parking garage, which was constructed in 1986.
The 2034 Olympics were also discussed, with some councilmembers saying the event puts pressure on making decisions and moving forward in order to avoid a major construction site in the center of town during the Games.
The conversation did not result in a final decision, but council members generally supported looking at Swede Alley as a broader district rather than treating China Bridge as an isolated parking project. Staff were directed to return with additional planning and financial analysis to help determine what that could look like.
The discussion built on conversations council has been having about the future of Historic Main Street Area Plan, which have included conversations on how to improve pedestrian circulation, transportation, and economic activity in the area.
Since completing the 2024 China Bridge structural assessment, the city has invested approximately $1.9 million in structural repairs, protective improvements, and operational upgrades, according to city staff. And replacing the southern structure with comparable parking that meets current code requirements is estimated at $14–19 million in current dollars. Staff estimated that replacement in 2030 or 2031 could cost approximately $16 million to $22 million.
A replacement project would likely require two construction seasons, staff said, with the timing and duration of a garage closure dependent on the city’s broader plans for downtown parking and construction.
While the southern portion of the garage was building 40 years ago, the northern structure was just built in 2006. Although the two structures operate as a single parking facility, their differing ages and conditions provide flexibility in planning the property’s future, according to staff.
There lies the second option: use the southern portion’s needed replacement as a catalyst for a larger redevelopment of city-owned property along Swede Alley.
Under that approach, the city could combine parking with commercial development, public gathering spaces, and transportation improvements. The discussion also raised questions about the future of nearby city-owned properties, including the Old Town Transit Center, Marsac parking areas, and other parcels along Swede Alley.
Staff also noted that private development could also help offset some of the cost of replacing the garage.
The next phase will require additional analysis of the district’s potential uses, the role of private investment, the public benefits the city wants to achieve, and the timing of any major construction.
What ideas do you have for making the Swede Alley corridor a more vibrant and welcoming community space?
Contact: heather@townlift.com
Heather Bergeson is a writer and editor based in Utah. Heather has written about travel, sports, business and the outdoors for Utah Life magazine, Utah Business magazine and Moab Sun News. She has a bachelor's degree in English and editing from Brigham Young University.

articles.title_orig: Dow tumbles more than 600 points as oil prices rise and market sell-off hits most sectors
articles.title_zh: Dow tumbles more than 600 points as oil prices rise and market sell-off hits most sectors
articles.content_orig:
The FTSE 100 has slumped after the UK’s borrowing costs climbed to their highest level since 1998.
Britain’s flagship stock index declined as much as 2pc on Thursday in its worst performance since May. Banks pushed the stock index lower as the financial sector was rocked by the bond sell-off.
Yields on 30-year gilts, which determine the interest the Treasury pays to borrow over that period, broke above 6pc for the first time in 28 years.
It marked the first time that any G7 nation has faced an interest rate of more than 6pc on its debt since Italy during the eurozone debt crisis in 2012.
Traders fear that a prolonged Iran war energy price shock will limit economic growth and force central banks to raise interest rates.
The Bank of England is expected to increase borrowing costs in November ahead of a predicted surge in energy bills over winter. Markets are betting that UK interest rates will hit 4.75pc by July next year.
Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, ordered Iranian negotiators to leave the US overnight after the two sides failed to make progress on an end to the conflict.
Tensions in the Middle East were raised further by an attempted hijacking of a plane carrying Israeli passengers to Tel Aviv on Wednesday.
Mohit Kumar, an economist at Jefferies, said: “US-Iran talks remained in stalemate. Reports of a possible hijacking of a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight brought back concerns over increasing risk of terrorism.”
The 10-year US Treasury bond yield – a benchmark for the cost of government borrowing around the world – jumped to 5.33pc, a level it last reached in 2002.
Read the latest updates below.
Thank you for following our live updates of today’s bond sell-off and the slump in the stock markets.
Taking a look at the FTSE 100, the index is down 1.68pc for the day as bank stocks pull lower.
The yield on 30-year gilts has fallen back slightly to 5.93pc after topping 6pc earlier, the highest level since 1998.
You can stay up to date with all the latest business news here.
UK bank stocks dropped sharply on Thursday, as 30-year gilts reached their highest levels since 1998.
Major lenders saw heavy losses, as NatWest fell 5.2pc, Lloyds dropped 4.4pc, and HSBC lost 4.3pc.
Barclays also slid nearly 4pc, as the FTSE 350 pulled lower in the afternoon session to 4.1pc.
The sell-off intensified following reports that top bank executives were summoned to meet John Healey ahead of the Budget, fuelling speculation about potential new taxes on the sector.
Earlier this week, Revolut was amongst a group of banks urging the chancellor to rules out tax rises on the sector.
Accenture shares have surged by 24pc after it beat forecasts, posting an 8pc rise in profits.
The consultancy, which employs 800,000 staff, has seen its stock slump sharply over the past few years over concern about the impacts of AI on its business.
However, Julie Sweet, its CEO, told a conference call that Accenture was boosted by demand for advice on AI and that the tech was making it more efficient.
Accenture is also investing in AI safety, in expectation that there will be a big growth in the sector, Ms Sweet said.
The Bank of England must raise interest rates to “maintain credibility” in the battle against inflation, a top policymaker has warned.
Catherine Mann, a member of the Monetary Policy Committee, said that at a time of rising inflation risks and the volatile war in Iran, it is important the Bank sets out its intentions clearly.
“Given rising upside risks to inflation, a risk management strategy to monetary policy is appropriate.
“When there is uncertainty about inflation dynamics and second-round effects, raising Bank Rate to commit to the inflation target can help ensure a sustainable return of inflation to the 2pc target, with smaller losses to economic activity,” she said.
“With the ‘sporadic continuance’ of the conflict in the Middle East, uncertainty around the outlook for the economy and inflation risks have remained elevated. Uncertainty about the MPC reaction function should not compound the problem.”
Inflation has so far risen to 3.1pc and is expected to rise above 4pc early next year.
Diesel prices are at a record high of around £2 per litre, while household energy bills are projected to rise by a further 16pc in January.
In turn this raises the danger of inflation spreading through more of the economy.
Ms Mann backed an increase in the Bank’s base rate from 3.75pc to 4pc in the past two MPC meetings, but was outvoted by the majority of the nine-strong panel.
“At some point, we need to follow through with Bank Rate rises – to maintain credibility, and to avoid policy expectations repricing downwards and inflation expectations repricing further upwards,” she said.
John Healey will meet with the chief executives of Britain’s banks next Tuesday ahead of his upcoming Budget.
Bosses from HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest, Santander UK, and Nationwide are amongst those summoned for talks with the chancellor, according to Sky News.
The meeting comes amidst growing industry anxiety over a potential bank tax raid in October.
The gathering will follow Mr Healey’s recent address at the Labour Party conference, where he pledged to work “in partnership with business and the unions”.
Unions have called on the chancellor to raise billions from the banks to help fund public services, given recent profits made by the sector.
The rally on Wall Street has been short lived after a spike in oil prices.
US stocks turned lower after the price of Brent crude climbed 3pc to nearly $101 a barrel, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 0.4pc.
The FTSE 100 was last down 1.5pc, while the Cac 40 in France fell 1.2pc.
The US stock market rallied at the open despite the pressure on bond markets.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5pc to 51,139.14 and the S&P 500 climbed 0.3pc to 7,674.66 even after the US 10-year Treasury bond yield hit its highest level since 2002.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite jumped 0.5pc to 26,999.09 after strong results from Micron boosted chip companies.
Opposition parties have questioned the Prime Minister’s handle on the recent rise in government borrowing costs.
Alex Burghart, the Tory deputy leader, told BBC Radio Kent: “We cannot afford to live like this.
“I was very worried to listen to Andy Burnham’s speech in Liverpool, where he had no plans to control government spending at all, and it’s like he’s not sort of looking at the financial markets in any way.”
Reform leader Nigel Farage said the Prime Minister “is not facing up to the reality that he can’t solve this crisis”.
The party’s economic spokesman Robert Jenrick suggested Mr Burnham would fail to curb borrowing costs with “unfunded promises on a National Care Service, a ballooning benefits bill and more delays for Heathrow”.
With the yield on 30-year US government debt at its highest since 2002, an obvious question to ask is why the stock market is so relaxed.
The cost of borrowing is back where it was before the financial crisis, bonds offer investors a viable alternative source of income again and the present-day value of future earnings is being squeezed. Why then are shares close to their all-time high ?
The obvious answer is that earnings continue to rise. We have had quarter after quarter of robust profits growth. Maybe that is reason enough. But even a cursory glance at history suggests that soaring bond yields can be the trigger for a stock market correction. The question remains: how high is too high for bond yields?
The global bond rout has abated in afternoon trading.
The yield on 10-year UK gilts sits 5.4pc, having risen as high as 5.5pc earlier, while the 30-year yield has eased back to 5.93pc, from as high as 6.02pc earlier.
France’s 10-year yield earlier closed in on the symbolic 5pc amid concerns over its unsustainable public finances. It touched 4.96pc earlier, its highest level since 2002, but has fallen back to 4.81pc.

articles.title_orig: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.title_zh: Duchess of Sussex was told of ‘disturbing allegations’ against her father in 2018
articles.content_orig:
Meghan reveals she was made aware of ‘disturbing allegations’ against him in 2018 by Met police
The Duchess of Sussex has said she is “deeply distressed” over accusations involving child sexual abuse images against her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr, and revealed she was made aware of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018 by the Metropolitan police.
Meghan issued a statement after the Sun newspaper published claims that her half-brother Thomas Markle Jr alleged he had found a stash of images belonging to their father at his former home in the Philippines.
In an interview with the Daily Mail, Markle Sr denied possessing child sexual abuse images, calling the accusations “sick lies”.
It is understood that authorities in the UK previously told Meghan that allegations made about her father in a 2018 letter sent to Scotland Yard, and subsequently shared with her by the police, were being investigated.
Meghan was informed by the Met of the allegations in the summer shortly after her wedding, it is believed.
In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan said: “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.
“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection [Rasp]. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them. I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”
Sources said although Meghan was made aware of the allegations in 2018, she had been unable to speak publicly to avoid jeopardising any future investigation and because speaking out could have resulted in legal action against her.
The 2018 letter was understood to have been shared with Meghan by the Rasp unit within the Met police.
It is understood the Met has not previously investigated Markle Sr, nor is it currently doing so. The force said it was making internal inquiries regarding officers from Rasp being involved in the passing on of a letter.
A Met spokesperson said: “We are aware of media reports that officers from the Met’s royalty and specialist protection command were involved in the passing on of a letter in 2018. We are undertaking inquiries internally in an effort to confirm this.”
Markle Sr has been estranged from the duchess since he failed to attend her wedding to Prince Harry on health grounds, and he has never met his grandchildren Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five.
The Sun reported that Markle Jr told detectives in the Philippines he had discovered “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sexual abuse images on computers and mobile phones stored in four large boxes at the home in Cebu where Markle Sr was living until he returned to the US in May after having a stroke.
Markle Jr, 60, said he had also contacted the FBI in the US, the Sun reported.
The FBI said in a statement: “The FBI is aware of the allegations and will provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of US law.”
The undersecretary for the Philippines’ justice department, Nicholas Ty, told the BBC the matter was being investigated by a human trafficking and child sexual exploitation taskforce in Cebu.
The interior secretary, Jonvic Remulla, separately told the BBC that national police had secured Markle Sr’s computer to conduct a comprehensive digital forensic examination. Remulla said it would take “one week to get the forensic [results]”.
Meghan’s father has denied possessing child sexual abuse images, telling the Daily Mail that the accusations were “sick lies”.
He told the newspaper that the computers had not been in his possession since he left Rosarito, Mexico, with his son in January 2025 and moved to the Philippines “for a fresh start”.
Speaking from a rehabilitation centre in Florida, where he is learning to walk with a prosthetic limb after his left leg was amputated because of a blood clot, he told the Mail: “I’m shocked, I’m hurt and I’m very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I’m being accused of. It’s the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.
“This is bullshit. It’s just a bunch of lies. It’s sick. I have no idea why Tom is trying to destroy me with these lies.”
Meghan’s half-sister Samantha Markle has defended their father, accusing her brother Markle Jr of “making up lies” to make money.
She told the Mail: “There is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever and my brother is disgusting for making them up. He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
She alleged her brother made the allegations days after their father cut off his funds, “and once the money stopped he made up the most outrageous lies he could to make money from the media”.
She alleged the computers were not in her father’s possession for two years and he could have been set up. “That leaves a lot of room for tampering,” she said.

articles.title_orig: ‘Black October’: cybersecurity experts sound the alarm over new era of AI-enabled hacking
articles.title_zh: ‘Black October’: cybersecurity experts sound the alarm over new era of AI-enabled hacking
articles.content_orig:
After discovery of severe bug in the PHP programming language, executives warn of ‘vulnerability tsunami’
Leaders in cybersecurity are sounding the alarm after the discovery of a major vulnerability this week. They are predicting that artificial intelligence tools will expose more fundamental weaknesses in global internet infrastructure in the months to come.
“I no longer think we’re going to be able to patch all bugs,” said Sam Altman on Thursday evening, joining the chorus of executives. In the midst of what’s being called “Black October”, for which researchers used AI to help identify critical flaws in a coding language that is used across millions of websites and may have been unpatched for years, tech executives are warning about the ways AI will be used both to identify and exploit security vulnerabilities at an unprecedented scale and pace.
The next few months will see a “vulnerability tsunami”, according to Jason Clinton, Anthropic’s deputy chief information security officer. “There won’t be enough time to patch critical infrastructure,” Clinton said in a post on X on Thursday evening. Marc Benioff, the Salesforce CEO, agreed and called it a “code red”.
AI is uniquely able to find and identify security flaws in a way and at a pace that will feel catastrophic because the security community will not be able to move quickly enough to address them, said Matthew Prince, the Cloudflare CEO. “It’s going to feel like the sky is falling. It’s going to feel like there’s nothing we can do.
“The next two years are going to be incredibly, incredibly, incredibly fraught with new tools that have infinite patience to go look for vulnerabilities across the Internet,” he wrote in a post on X.
While cybersecurity experts have been warning about a “vulnpocalypse”, or the ability for AI to more easily identify security bugs for months, it wasn’t until “Black October” that researchers were able to use AI to find a flaw as fundamental and critical as the one announced on 21 October.
Massive bugs were found in a programming language called PHP, which may have left the millions of websites that run on it vulnerable to hackers for years. Some experts estimated 70% of all the sites on the internet were at risk of hacking.
However, in the same way AI will be used to aid in identifying security vulnerabilities at an unprecedented pace, tech leaders worry it’ll also be used by malicious actors to exploit those bugs at an unprecedented pace.
Attempts to exploit the PHP vulnerability have already begun .
After the vulnerabilities were announced, government and private websites across the US and UK temporarily took down their sites to patch the bugs. The US National Security Agency (NSA) issued an alert recommending any site that runs on PHP implement the patches immediately. Malicious cyberactors may seek to further exploit these bugs to access servers without authorization, the NSA said.
“Such an access vector could help attackers steal sensitive data, disrupt services or move deeper into a network,” the warning read.
after newsletter promotion
In a post on X, Prince said CloudFlare, a security provider, had seen evidence of thousands of people trying to exploit the PHP flaws in the 10 hours before it was announced.
“That jumped to tens of thousands in the 45 minutes post announcement, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours, and millions now,” he wrote.
In a blogpost, researchers at AI security platform Wiz said that this was “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history”.
“The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” they wrote.

articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Opens Lower, Oil Prices Hit 5-Month High — Live Updates
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Opens Lower, Oil Prices Hit 5-Month High — Live Updates
articles.content_orig:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was in India this week
The western Indian port town of Jamnagar is not a usual stop for foreign leaders, yet it featured prominently in US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's recent visit.
So, why did Rubio visit the town? And, more importantly, why did he skip the Indian capital, Delhi?
The answer to both questions may have less to do with India and more to do with Donald Trump administration's domestic compulsions â or, more precisely, its domestic oil needs.
Rubio arrived in the financial capital Mumbai on Tuesday, where he met Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar and some of the country's top business leaders. He officially ended his trip in Jamnagar - in the western state of Gujarat - home to the giant oil refinery owned by one of Asia's richest men, Mukesh Ambani.
It was his second trip to the country this year and experts say what is significant this time is the timing of the visit as well as his choice of destinations.
The Trump administration is under pressure to keep fuel prices in check ahead of November's US midterm elections, while rising tensions in the Middle East threaten global energy supplies.
With little new refining capacity expected in the immediate future in the US, India's ability to process large volumes of crude oil offers Washington a potential way to ease pressure on the fuel markets.
And that puts Reliance's Jamnagar refinery at the centre of the equation.
The visit, however, comes at a tricky moment in India-US relations. Trump has imposed tariffs on Indian goods, there are sanctions against Delhi for buying Russian energy (though currently paused) and there is a trade deal between the two countries that has remained elusive for around 20 months now.
Rubio (left) held talks with foreign minister S Jaishankar (right) in Mumbai
Announcing the visit, the US State Department had earlier said that it would focus on energy cooperation, commercial investment and economic ties.
The official itinerary also did not include Delhi, which raised some questions, especially from Indian opposition politicians. But analysts say the choice was strategic.
"Delhi is where the trust gap is largest. Officials there are unhappy with a number of decisions and policies from Trump's administration," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, told the BBC.
But former Indian ambassador to the US, Meera Shankar, cautions against reading too much into him skipping the capital.
"This was primarily an energy-focused visit," she says. "And after all, Rubio did meet the foreign minister in Mumbai."
The meeting between the two foreign ministers at the Taj Hotel covered trade, investment, energy security and defence cooperation, according to official statements. India's foreign ministry also said both sides welcomed progress in trade negotiations and reaffirmed their commitment to concluding a deal, which has long been in the works.
But once the diplomatic meetings were over, Rubio headed to Jamnagar, where the crown jewel of the Ambani business empire is located. This came to define the trip.
Shankar says the refinery visit "showed how much importance the US is attaching to getting more refined fuel into the market before the November midterms".
Reliance's Jamnagar complex can process about 1.4 million barrels of crude oil a day, roughly 1.5% of global refining capacity, according to the company website.
It is also a major exporter of diesel and other petroleum products, giving it a crucial role in global fuel markets.
During a tightly controlled visit on Wednesday, with limited media access, Rubio toured the facility and met members of the Ambani family, including Mukesh Ambani.
The company later released a statement, saying, "the visit included wide-ranging discussions on the global energy landscape and opportunities for commercial partnerships across conventional and new energy". It, however, did not specifically address any commitments to buy crude oil or supply refined products.
Just a day earlier, while speaking to the press, Rubio had called India a "refining superpower" and said the US wanted Reliance to process more Venezuelan oil.
"They have the capability to refine heavy crude. They've done so in the past, and I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, that's something they could do," he told reporters.
Rubio added that oil from Venezuela "can certainly provide relief" in the short term and can possibly help ease supply pressures amid tensions in the Middle East.
Reliance was once among the largest buyers of Venezuelan crude before US sanctions disrupted trade. After Venezuelan President NicolÃ¡s Maduro was captured in a US intervention earlier this year and Washington eased sanctions on the country's energy sector, Reliance re-emerged as a major importer.
Rubio's visit to the Jamnagar refinery was closed to the media, with images released afterwards by the Reliance Group
Experts also say the visit might ease some tensions in the Delhi-Washington relationship over India's purchase of Russian oil.
India became one of the biggest buyers of Russian oil since Moscow invaded Ukraine in 2022.
Between December 2022 and July 2026, it accounted for 37% of Russia's crude oil exports, according to the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA).
And Reliance was among the Indian companies that processed Russian crude.
In August 2025, US President Donald Trump imposed an additional 25% tariff on Indian goods over its Russian oil purchases, taking total tariffs on many Indian goods to 50%. The US, however, withdrew the additional penalty in February 2026 but India's import of Russian oil has continued to be an irritant in Washington-Delhi ties.
India has always said that securing affordable and reliable energy for its 1.4 billion people was its priority.
Then  earlier this month, the US itself temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.
In that context, experts say Rubio's Jamnagar visit is aligned to three goals that the US appears to be pursuing: reducing India's dependence on Russian crude, encouraging greater imports of Venezuelan and American oil, and advancing a trade deal in which energy cooperation could become a key area of agreement.
There is also another possible business angle behind this push.
Kugelman says Rubio had two reasons to meet the Ambani family. First, to secure greater refining of Venezuelan oil and second to seek assurances that Reliance remained interested in backing a proposed Texas refinery.
In March, Trump announced a proposed refinery at the Port of Brownsville in Texas on his Truth Social platform. He said that it would be the first major new refinery in the US in 50 years.
Reliance has not publicly commented on it and there are no details on the project or when the work is expected to begin.
"The Texas facility may not be as immediately important to US interests as the arrangement tied to Venezuelan oil, but I still think it's part of the story," he says.
Trump hopes to bring down gas prices as the US heads to midterms next month
However, analysts point out that closer cooperation with Reliance and progress on energy security do not necessarily mean a trade deal is imminent.
"I don't think anyone really expected a trade deal to be announced at this point, but this trip seems to have helped get the relationship back on track, to the extent that it can, given the significant points of tension that remain," Kugelman said.
Rajani Sinha, the chief economist at credit rating agency CareEdge, told the BBC that greater cooperation could allay energy security concerns in both countries, help push the stalled trade negotiations forward and "boost trade and sentiment" in India.
Meera Shankar says that India is possibly "waiting for the US to formalise its tariff positions so that we know whether Delhi has a preferential trade deal".
She adds that, although ties between the two countries have been strained in recent times, their bilateral trade continues to grow.

articles.title_orig: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.title_zh: Russia, Ukraine agree to ceasefire in Ukrainian city hit by food crisis, brokered by Melania Trump
articles.content_orig:
U.S. first lady Melania Trump has secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said on Friday.
Residents of the southern Ukrainian town, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, have reported a deepening food crisis.
"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," a White House statement said.
The development comes as Melania Trump's husband, President Donald Trump, pressures Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which began when Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022.
Melania Trump has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.
"The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water," Melania Trump said in the statement.
The ceasefire will allow non-military teams from both countries to visit residents in their homes and coordinate transportation for those wishing to evacuate to either Russia or Ukraine, with an unnamed media organization accompanying the teams to document the process, the first lady said.
Newsmax, a right-leaning news outlet, said in a report that its cameras would be granted "exclusive access to document the effort."
Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from Kherson, has a remaining population of 1,700 to 2,000 people — primarily elderly residents, along with about 50 children — down from roughly 24,000 before the war, the White House said. About 90% of the city was flooded following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, according to the White House.
The statement said Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine," Melania Trump said.

articles.title_orig: Gov. Kemp: Mitsubishi Power's $490 million Chatham County expansion to create 220 jobs
articles.title_zh: Gov. Kemp: Mitsubishi Power's $490 million Chatham County expansion to create 220 jobs
articles.content_orig:
Above video: Your Friday headlines
Mitsubishi Power Americas plans to invest $490 million to expand its manufacturing operation in Chatham County, adding more than 220 jobs and nearly doubling the facility’s footprint, Georgia Gov. Brian Kemp announced Friday.
The company will add 450,000 square feet to its Savannah Machinery Works facility at 1000 Pine Meadow Drive near Pooler. The plant, visible to drivers traveling along Interstate 16, manufactures and assembles gas turbines used to generate electricity for homes and businesses.
Mitsubishi Power said the expanded facility is expected to begin operating in early 2029.
“The expansion includes a 450,000-square-foot increase in our footprint here at the site, an additional 220 new jobs for the region and advancements in manufacturing technology and overall capacity,” said Brandon Bodie, vice president of Savannah Machinery Works.
The company expects to hire workers for positions in manufacturing, engineering, quality control, maintenance, logistics, operations and heavy machinery.
Local leaders said they hope to fill the temporary construction jobs and permanent positions with people who already live in the region.
Hugh “Trip” Tollison, president and CEO of the Savannah Economic Development Authority, said the project’s economic impact will begin before the expansion opens.
“When you think about a half-billion dollars going into one construction project, think about the labor that’s going to be needed to build the building and the concrete that’s going to be poured,” Tollison said.
He called the expansion a major win for Chatham County and said it was a highly competitive project.
“This is the largest investment to date on behalf of Mitsubishi Power Americas and will create meaningful new job opportunities for our community,” Tollison said.
Mitsubishi Power said it is expanding to keep pace with rising demand for electricity and power-generation equipment.
The company provides equipment and services for the energy industry, including gas, steam and aero-derivative turbines, geothermal systems and environmental controls. It also develops artificial intelligence technology designed to support autonomous power plant operations.
Bill Newsom, president and CEO of Mitsubishi Power Americas, said the expansion will strengthen domestic manufacturing while giving employees access to more advanced technology.
“This expansion strengthens American manufacturing and gives our people the advanced capabilities they need as they continue to deliver for our customers,” Newsom said.
Bodie said the company is also focused on developing a skilled local workforce.
“We’re excited about building a really strong workforce here that’s skilled and can support manufacturing in this community,” he said.
Mitsubishi Power has operated in Chatham County since 2009, when it established the Savannah Machinery Works operation during the Great Recession.
The expansion follows meetings Kemp and other state officials held with Mitsubishi Power and its parent company, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, in Tokyo.
“We are excited that the Savannah Machinery Works is expanding to turn those possibilities into reality,” Kemp said in a statement.
Georgia Economic Development Commissioner Pat Wilson said the state’s ports, railroads, highways and airports helped make the area attractive for the project. He also credited Georgia’s longstanding relationship with Mitsubishi Power.
“As demand for Mitsubishi Power’s products grows, this expansion is a reminder that economic development is about more than winning a project,” Wilson said. “It is about showing up, building relationships and being a long-term partner.”
The Georgia Department of Economic Development coordinated the project with the Savannah Economic Development Authority, Georgia Power and Georgia Quick Start.
Additional details about the construction and hiring schedules were not immediately available.

articles.title_orig: Crackgate? iPhone Duo Owners Report Screens Breaking Along the Hinge
articles.title_zh: Crackgate? iPhone Duo Owners Report Screens Breaking Along the Hinge
articles.content_orig:
Some iPhone Duos are already experiencing hinge issues that cause display cracks, based on photos shared on Reddit and the MacRumors forums . Almost all of the display faults are right along the hinge, and most result in a line of bright pixels across one side of the screen.
An iPhone Duo owner in Australia said his device cracked after being opened fewer than 20 times, and there was no visible damage beforehand.
Had my iPhone Duo for about six hours and had probably opened it fewer than 20 times. I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen.
As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge. There were no marks or damage on the inner screen's surface or the external hinge to suggest anything had been caught or damaged.
The user visited an Apple Store , and Apple replaced the broken device right away. Apple is likely collecting defective iPhone Duos to research points of failure, and that research could lead to manufacturing improvements to reduce future issues.
There are several images of broken displays from demo devices in China , where the ‌iPhone Duo‌ launched hours ahead of the U.S. The backstory for most of the images is unknown, and it's possible user damage is a factor. Some reviewers who got an ‌iPhone Duo‌ early subjected it to folding tests and didn't experience screen issues, but that's a small sample.
With so many people getting iPhone Duos today, some failures are expected. It isn't known how widespread the issue is or whether we'll see an uptick in complaints over time. Hinge failures from normal use should be covered under the one-year warranty, and customers receiving an ‌iPhone Duo‌ today will also have two weeks to make a return.

articles.title_orig: Treasury proposes major restrictions to U.S. investment in Chinese biotech sector
articles.title_zh: Treasury proposes major restrictions to U.S. investment in Chinese biotech sector
articles.content_orig:
By John Wilkerson and Damian Garde
John writes about the politics of health care, and he is the author of the twice-weekly D.C. Diagnosis newsletter . You can reach John on Signal at John_Wilkerson.07.
Damian covers the global drug industry and contributes to STAT’s industry-leading events. You can reach Damian on Signal at damiangarde.67.
WASHINGTON — The Trump administration late on Thursday proposed a rule that would severely restrict future U.S. investment in the Chinese biotech sector but still allow American drugmakers to buy the rights to medicines invented in the country.
The Treasury Department proposed the rule to implement a law, called the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, that restricts U.S. investment in industries of concern to national security. The department added biotechnology to the list of industries subject to COINS restrictions, joining the likes of semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and quantum technology.
The proposal would prohibit U.S. companies from entering financial transactions with Chinese biotech companies or Chinese manufacturers of biotechnology-related equipment and tools, according to the research firm Veda.

articles.title_orig: Mother drowns trying to save sons during Bahamas snorkeling trip
articles.title_zh: Mother drowns trying to save sons during Bahamas snorkeling trip
articles.content_orig:
A doting mother drowned while desperately trying to rescue her two children who were swept away by a strong current while snorkeling in the Bahamas, according to a report.
The 36-year-old unidentified British woman was on a snorkeling expedition with her husband and two sons south of the island of Bimini when the tragedy occurred on Tuesday, The Tribune reported .
The children were washed up by a strong current — so the mom rushed to save them, but was swept away herself, according to the outlet.
Rescuers pulled her from the water and performed CPR at a ferry dock, but the woman died at the hospital, the spokesperson said.
Linty Stuart, the owner of L&A Water Taxi, captained the boat that saved the boys and pulled the hero mom out of the water, according to the ZNS Network .
“It happened, really really fast. I’m still in shock too,” Stuart told the station, adding that big waves made the rescue difficult.
“It’s scary. We tried … It’s sad,” added first mate Jason Saunders.
The family was reportedly visiting the tropical island from a cruise ship.
The Royal Bahamas Police Force did not immediately respond to a request for information from The Post.

articles.title_orig: Xi Jinping May Have His Own Reasons to Avert a China-Russia-US Summit - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: Xi Jinping May Have His Own Reasons to Avert a China-Russia-US Summit - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin have put Xi Jinping in an unusual position by expressing interest in a trilateral summit with the Chinese leader at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen mid-November. Xi’s cautious response so far – Moscow and Washington have confirmed discussion, while Beijing has yet to commit publicly – could help Europe and Ukraine avoid the worst: major powers making decisions about the region in their absence.
The idea for a meeting came from Russia and it’s not hard to see why. Moscow’s ideal outcome would reportedly be a “Yalta-style” agreement on Ukraine, echoing the 1945 conference at which the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union discussed the post-war order in Europe. But even much more modest results would count as a success. Simply taking part in such a summit would elevate Russia’s status alongside the U.S. and China, help break its diplomatic isolation, potentially drive a further wedge between the U.S. and Europe, and provide an important platform for its narrative of Western threats to Russia.
A three-way meeting would play to Trump’s self-regard as a dealmaker and peacemaker – and quite possibly his appetite for economic gain. The United States recently eased sanctions on Russian diesel fuel exports, with an initial shipment of 40,000 tonnes reportedly on its way to the U.S. Moscow has also offered to increase fertilizer exports amid shortages caused by the Middle East crisis. But Trump may also have a larger strategic motivation. He has said that nuclear disarmament , not Ukraine, should be at the top of the agenda.
With the APEC summit in China being discussed as the venue, Xi would surely welcome the huge symbolic win of being seen as the world leader capable of hosting such an important gathering – while possibly helping to widen the divide between the U.S. and Europe. But Xi also has very good reasons to avoid such a meeting. China has benefited from dealing with Washington and Moscow separately, and it has in the past insisted that both Russia and Ukraine must be involved in any peace process. A China-Russia-U.S. summit to discuss Ukraine’s future without Kyiv would undermine both those positions.
A high-profile trilateral could overshadow the APEC summit, which Beijing wants to use to showcase its economic leadership and promote openness, innovation, and cooperation . A highly publicized gathering of three major powers also would sit uneasily with Beijing’s repeated calls for inclusive multilateralism, particularly at a forum intended to promote regional economic cooperation.
A successful trilateral might make the risk worthwhile. But such an outcome is uncertain – not least because of the unpredictability of Trump and Putin. The meeting could end up dominating APEC at the expense of Beijing’s economic agenda, without producing any significant outcomes.
Lastly, while Putin and Trump have major strategic incentives to meet, Xi has a strategic reason to avoid doing so. Trump’s insistence on putting nuclear arms reduction at the top of the agenda is problematic for China. Beijing has long emphasized that its nuclear arsenal is far smaller than those of the United States and Russia – and that Washington and Moscow must make substantial reductions before China joins any talks. Abandoning this position would risk China being bound by the same rules as Russia and the U.S., despite the gap in nuclear capabilities.
But Xi may recognize that he cannot dismiss the idea of a meeting altogether. Chinese diplomats have reportedly indicated that they would not rule out a trilateral. If Xi cannot prevent such a meeting, he could at least use his position as host to shape it – a less prominent, more informal encounter with a loose agenda focused on major power relations or the global economy, rather than a formal summit focused on Ukraine or nuclear arms control that would raise public expectations. Xi could even cast himself as the host of a Trump-Putin meeting rather than a participant in three-way talks.
Such stage-management would not protect Europe and Ukraine from the United States, Russia, and China talking about them behind their backs. But it would allow European governments to frame such a meeting as nothing more than an exchange of views. A formal summit explicitly devoted to Ukraine, by contrast, would risk signaling to the world that the three leaders are entitled – by right or by force – to make strategic decisions about Europe in Europe’s absence. That alone would send a terrible precedent for the continent.
Much can still happen until the APEC summit next month. Another round of U.S.-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi are reportedly under discussion, while Trump’s views on Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy continue to shift. But whatever summitry emerges in Shenzhen, European governments must continue to insist on Ukrainian participation in any talks about the country’s future. Apart from pressing Washington to take them into account, Kyiv and European capitals should also appeal to Xi’s own reservations about a trilateral summit that also carries many risks for Beijing.

articles.title_orig: News - Who Crafted China’s Terracotta Army?
articles.title_zh: News - Who Crafted China’s Terracotta Army?
articles.content_orig:
XI’AN, CHINA— Science Alert reports that an analysis of fingerprints preserved in the clay of a sample of soldiers from the Terracotta Army suggests that men, women, and children contributed to the work of assembling the sculptures. Discovered in 1974 by farmers digging a well about a mile away from the 2,200-year-old tomb of China’s Emperor Qin Shihuangdi, the Terracotta Army is made up of approximately 8,000 soldier statues bearing a wide variety of faces, hairstyles, and armor. Thirty-six warrior statues recovered from the same pit were surveyed for the study, and a total of 91 fingerprints were identified on them. Twelve of these prints were excluded because they seemed to come from individuals who left multiple prints. Of the 79 remaining fingerprints, 73 were left behind during the process of molding, shaping, and assembling the statues. Most of these prints were found on the warriors’ heads and arms. The other six fingerprints were left behind during the decorating process, and were found on nails and waistbands of the soldiers’ armor. The distances between the ridges of fingerprints can be used as clues to the age and sex of the person, and so a mathematical model was used to estimate who might have worked on these 36 statues. About 45 percent of the prints are thought to have belonged to men, 32 percent to women, and about 22 percent to children under the age of 15. The teens may have been working as apprentices, as described in Qin Dynasty records. “These findings challenge the long-held assumption that Terracotta Army production relied exclusively on adult male labor,” said Xiaoxi Li of the Emperor Qin Shihuang Mausoleum Site Museum. articles.title_orig: Trump says Burnham is 'getting it done' after Jackdaw decision
articles.title_zh: Trump says Burnham is 'getting it done' after Jackdaw decision
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump has praised Prime Minister Andy Burnham for the UK government's decision to approve production from the North Sea's Jackdaw gas field.
He said he had spoken with Burnham, telling reporters on Friday that the decision would "make the UK a very rich country".
Trump said: "The other prime minister, the previous man, Starmer. He's a very nice man, but he never got it done, and this one is getting it."
The decision had been subject to intense debate around its environment and economic impact and came after years of legal challenges.
Burnham announced the decision to approve the drilling of the Jackdaw gas field earlier this week.
Jackdaw is situated 150 miles (241km) east of Aberdeen and is operated by Adura, a joint venture between Shell and Norwegian state energy firm Equinor.
Ministers said the first gas could be produced by the end of this month, helping heat millions of homes, and also announced the creation of a new energy wealth fund.
Environmental campaigners say the decision would hamper efforts to tackle climate change and make "no meaningful difference" to UK energy security.
Based on official forecasts for the amount of gas the UK will need over the next decade, that suggests Jackdaw has the potential to meet around 1.6% of total projected national gas demand between 2026 and 2036.
Operators say it could be connected to the Great British gas network within weeks and could produce gas for the next 11 years.
Trump responded to the decision on Friday, but appeared to confuse oil and gas.
He said: "They're opening up the North Sea oil. I've been after them to do that for two years."
Trump added: "Andy is getting it done, and I guess it's against the liberal principle, but he knows what's right. It's going to make UK a very wealthy country."
In a discussion on Friday, Burnham and Trump spoke about the decision to approve Jackdaw.
The two leaders "agreed on the significant benefits this will bring to the UK, boosting the economy and supporting jobs for British workers", a statement from Number 10 read.
It added that Trump and Burnham "welcomed the continued collaboration between UK and US companies, especially on nuclear power".
Earlier this week, on Wednesday, Trump said the decision was "great news for the wealth and prosperity" of the UK.
Writing on his Truth Social platform, Trump urged the UK to go "full blast" and called the North Sea "one of the greatest and most prosperous areas of oil in the world".
A decision is yet to be taken on whether production can begin at Rosebank, the UK's largest known untapped oil field, which is located off the coast of Shetland in the North Atlantic.
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused the prime minister of "dithering" on Jackdaw and said a ban on new oil and gas licences should be repealed.
However, Burnham said her party had "messed up" the original decision by not giving any regard to climate obligations - things he said "have to be considered in the round".
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said gas from Jackdaw would be in homes and businesses this month, but that it would not lower energy bills this winter.
She said the decision was "compatible" with legally binding climate commitments, adding:  "We remain resolute in ending new licences for oil and gas and achieving net zero by 2050."
Environmental groups have criticised the Jackdaw approval. Areeba Hamid, the co-executive director of Greenpeace, said it was "the wrong decision" in terms of lowering energy bills, providing energy security, and addressing climate change.
Meanwhile, Oxfam said the government had "drilled straight through the UK's climate commitments".
During their Friday talks, Trump and Burnham spoke about the Falkland Islands and the Sea Lion oilfield project, a joint venture between British and Israeli companies.
In September, the Argentinian government threatened to impose economic sanctions on firms exploiting oil close to the Falkland Islands, and earlier this month, it began legal action to stop the exploration of oil and gas fields.
Burnham raised the "economic consequences of Argentina's coercive measures for the UK and US and reiterated the importance of respecting the Islanders' right to develop their natural resources", Downing Street said.
The two leaders also discussed Ukraine, with the prime minister underlining the importance for Ukraine "to have full access to Starlink so they can continue to defend themselves against Russia's full-scale invasion", according to Number 10.
Starlink technology is a satellite system owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company which Ukraine has relied upon during the war.
In recent days, Ukraine has been recording issues with the network , according to sources within the defence ministry. This has affected the country's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations.
The Downing Street statement added: "The Prime Minister recognised the work of President Trump to bring Putin to the negotiation table and the leaders agreed to work together, alongside international partners to bring an end to the bloodshed."

articles.title_orig: Why ‘Final Fantasy’ Returned To 2D
articles.title_zh: Why ‘Final Fantasy’ Returned To 2D
articles.content_orig:
It’s 1996. I’m happily traversing via chocobo and airship a magical world full of moogles, espers, crystals and magitek. I’m dazzled by the vibrant pixel art.
It’s 2026. I’m happily traversing via chocobo and airship a magical world full of moogles, espers, crystals and magitek. I’m dazzled by the vibrant pixel art.
FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE is the first time that Square Enix has applied its trademarked “HD-2D” style to its flagship franchise. Like in Triangle Strategy and the Octopath Traveler games, it combines expressive 2D pixel art sprites with 3D environments, cinematic cameras, dynamic lighting, particle effects, and depth of field into a compelling, hybrid aesthetic.
Several RPGs experimented with a similar look back on the PS1 (including Square’s own Xenogears ), and the HD-2D games aren’t so much a throwback as they are emissaries from a parallel universe where pixel art was never supplanted by full 3D and instead evolved. With nearly a decade of practice in the style, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE might be the best and most pushed it’s looked yet.
The story is an adaptation of FINAL FANTASY BRAVE EXVIUS , a free-to-play mobile gacha RPG that ran from 2015 to 2025, but this is no simple port or visual upgrade. Developers Square Enix and LANCARSE have built and balanced the combat/progression systems and world anew on top of that original story into a fully featured, single-player, single-purchase RPG. It’s a love letter to the series and a nostalgic return to its foundational roots with a modern upgrade, much like FINAL FANTASY IX did over 26 years ago.
FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE follows childhood friends Rain and Lasswell, knights for the idyllic Kingdom of Grandshelt. That idyll is shattered when a mysterious, powerful, armored man attacks the castle, steals a magical relic, and destroys the sacred Earth Crystal under the kingdom’s protection, throwing everything into chaos. Joined eventually by Fina, an amnesiac spellcaster with some connection to all of this,  and a party of unique individuals each with their own reason to stop the impending chaos, they set out to stop the Sworn Six from destroying the world’s other elemental Crystals, each protected in different lands.
Beyond being a visual throwback, this back-to-roots story is a direct return to the original style of archetypal fantasy narrative that dominated the first five entries in the series before FINAL FANTASY VI (my first and still personal favorite) started to really widen the dramatic and narrative scope of their storytelling ambitions. A party of four or more heroes endeavors to save the world-infrastructural elemental Crystals from some great peril. It’s a comfortable mythopoetic space that’s still very open-ended and easy to iterate for a classic-style RPG.
Like in the classic games, the high-fantasy melodrama of the overarching plot is balanced out by a brighter tone that’s often quite lighthearted from scene to scene. This levity keeps it fun and easy to play through but also helps land the heavier emotional beats by contrast.
In addition to returning to the series’ aesthetic and narrative roots, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE is also going back to classic, menu-driven combat. It’s not even Active-Time Battles, like the series iterated from FINAL FANTASY IV on, but fully turn-based, with a timeline on top of the screen showing the upcoming action order of allies and enemies. This adds a satisfyingly strategic layer to combat as you can preemptively react to the enemy, prioritizing targets and minimizing incoming harm.
A central new combat mechanic is that every enemy has a stagger meter. Every attack available to you indicates proportionally how much damage it does to both health and stagger. When you deplete an enemy’s stagger meter, they are stunned, losing their action for the round and taking more damage. The character that staggers an enemy gets a bonus action at the end of the round, and if you stagger every surviving enemy, you trigger a “sweeping stagger,” which gives your whole team a bonus end-of-round action.
Combined with a classic framework of elemental weakness/resistance and status effects (poison, blind, silence, charm, etc.), with targeting weaknesses doing more health and stagger damage, this creates a very satisfying old-school combat flow. Characters also progress in a very traditional fashion, gaining predetermined stats and a fixed, unique list of skills and spells as they level up.
Lest you worry about a lack of customization, however, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE has it in the form of Visions. These are the echoes of past FINAL FANTASY characters who lend Rain and his allies their powers in battle. So far, I’ve seen the Warrior of Light ( I ), Cloud ( VII ), Terra ( VI ) and Zidane ( IX ), with many more left to find scattered around the world in shrines. Each of your party members can have one Vision assigned at a time, gaining access to their abilities. Triggering a sweeping stagger also allows you to unleash its special Resonance attack, complete with a full 3D summon-style cutscene.
Fighting alongside Visions increases that character’s mastery level with them, unlocking more abilities, which can then be equipped up to a fixed point limit even with a different vision equipped. The combination of a character’s base skills and their Vision’s plus any others you’ve unlocked and equipped, gives quite a bit of latitude in how you construct each character’s kit, which I found myself situationally changing as I went to match the demands of whatever dungeon I was in.
It’s the most obvious echo of the game’s gacha roots in FINAL FANTASY BRAVE EXVIUS , but stripped of all randomness and monetization. What’s left is just the compelling hook of wanting to find more cool characters to play with, especially if, like me, you have a longstanding history with the games. FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE is very rewarding to fans in general, at every level chock-full of clever little nods and references to across the series’ whole history, like a bard you meet off-handedly describing himself as “spoony.”
Like so many of the best remakes and nostalgic media, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE succeeds by capturing your memory of the originals, rose-tinted glasses and all. All sorts of thoughtful little modernizations shave off those corners and bits of friction that can make the earlier games a little bit of a slog to replay. Enemy weaknesses and resistances are shown forever once you’ve found them, making it much easier to blaze through repeat combats, which are also accelerated by variable speed and skippable summon cutscenes. You can also avoid unnecessary random battles entirely by fast traveling to any previously visited location from outside of dungeons.
All these touches add up to make a smooth experience that respects my time. It’s a charming throwback, with a satisfying and thoughtful rhythm of play that I’ve missed in modern RPGs, but in a sleek and modern package. Throw in a bit of nostalgic fan service for good measure, and I expect to be enjoying this for quite a while.

articles.title_orig: Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by report alleging her dad possessed child sexual abuse images
articles.title_zh: Meghan ‘deeply distressed’ by report alleging her dad possessed child sexual abuse images
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex , said Friday that she was “deeply distressed” by a report alleging that her estranged father, Thomas Markle Sr. , possessed child sexual abuse images, adding that she was informed by police of “disturbing allegations” against him in 2018.
In a statement Friday, Meghan addressed the report that her father was being investigated over claims he kept child sexual abuse videos and images at his home in the Philippines. “The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” said Meghan, who has in recent years had a limited and fraught relationship with her father. He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, drawing widespread media scrutiny.
The allegations against Markle Sr. were first reported Thursday by The Sun newspaper, a British tabloid, which reported that his son had informed police after he said he found “hundreds, if not thousands” of child sex abuse images in boxes at his father’s home. The Sun published a photo it said showed his son, Thomas  Markle Jr., signing a sworn statement it said he had submitted to police and quoted him as saying: “I won’t speak to my father ever again unless I’m called to give evidence against him.”
Markle Sr., 82, denied the reported allegations, calling them “sick lies” in a statement to Britain’s Daily Mail newspaper. He added they were “the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.”
NBC News was not immediately able to identify a contact for  Markle Sr., who the Daily Mail reported was now in a Florida rehab center recovering from surgery.
Markle Jr. told the Sun that he had reported his discovery to the FBI, as well as local Philippine authorities. NBC News has reached out to the FBI for comment, which did not immediately respond.
The Philippines’ justice department confirmed Friday that “the matter is under investigation” but otherwise declined to “provide further details at this time.”
Police in Cebu City, the location of Markle Sr.’s home in the Philippines, and London’s Metropolitan Police did not immediately respond to requests for comment from NBC News.
In the rare statement Friday, Meghan said that she had chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father “for one reason: to protect them.”
“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” she said in the statement.
Meghan said that she had been made aware of a letter sent to the British police and other authorities in 2018, that “made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.”
“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them,” she added.
“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” Meghan said.
Asked by NBC News when Meghan was made aware of the letter to the Metropolitan Police, a spokesman for the couple said it was in the summer of 2018, after her wedding with Harry.
Separately, a source close to the couple told NBC News that Meghan’s decision not to speak publicly eight years ago should be understood in a particular context: “When she was made aware of these allegations in 2018 after they were reported to the police, they remained just that — allegations.”
“To have repeated them publicly at that stage would not only have potentially exposed her to civil action for making unsubstantiated claims, but she had also been advised that doing so could jeopardize any subsequent investigation,” the source added.
Markle Sr. told the Daily Mail he had not spoken to his son “for months” and said “these terrible lies are being made against me with no proof.” He added that he would “welcome an investigation” into the matter and labeled the accusations “a bunch of lies.”
His daughter, Samantha Markle, also told the Daily Mail of her brother’s allegations: “there is no merit in these disgusting allegations whatsoever ... He wants to destroy our dad. Shame on him.”
NBC News did not immediately receive responses to requests for comment from Markle Jr. or Samantha Markle — Meghan’s half-siblings.
Markle Sr. married Meghan’s mother, Doria Ragland, in 1979 and they subsequently divorced in 1987.
Meghan, 45, and Harry, 42, moved back to the United Kingdom earlier this summer after several years in the United States.
The couple made their first joint public appearance last week visiting charities in central England. King Charles III has made clear that their return does not signal a return to active royal life. Harry, however, has said recently that he wants his disagreements with his family to “work out.”
Adela Suliman is a breaking-news editor and reporter for NBC News in London.

articles.title_orig: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
articles.title_zh: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
articles.content_orig:
According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads.
According to the new terms, sharing your data for better AI recommendations also means opening it up for more personalized ads.
Google has updated its privacy policy in a way that could mean you’ll start seeing targeted ads based on your personal data if you’re using personalized AI features. The update, spotted by Android Authority , adds an exception to its promise about not using your Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos for personalized ads. While the previous version simply said it wouldn’t do that, as of October 16th, Google has added the line, “unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads.”
That means anyone who has connected their Drive, Gmail, or Google Photos to AI Mode and other Search tools via Google’s Personal Intelligence feature — allowing those tools to provide better responses or recommendations by knowing more about you — may now see ads targeted on the basis of that content.
Advertisers don’t get access to your Drive, Gmail, and Photos information or personally identifying details such as your name or email address, and Google won’t show you ads based on sensitive categories like race, sexual orientation, religion, or health.
This is what the policy says:
“You may choose to allow certain Google services, including services like Search or Gemini Apps, to access data from other Google services you use, such as Google Photos and Workspace apps like Gmail and Drive, in order to provide you with a more personalized experience, subject to the policies and settings of the accessing service. For example, Search may process some of the data that you allow Search to access to personalize content, including ads.”
“Depending on your settings, we may also show you personalized ads based on your interests, activity, or personalized content from Google services. For example, if you search for ‘mountain bikes,’ in Search you may see ads for sports equipment on YouTube.”
If you want to prevent your personal data from being used for targeted ads, you can choose which apps you want to disconnect from Search’s Personal Intelligence features or disable Personalized Recommendations entirely via the Search Services Personalization settings page.

articles.title_orig: Trump Blasts Vanity Fair Over ‘Fake News’ On Jared Kushner’s Alleged Undisclosed Foreign Bank Accounts
articles.title_zh: Trump Blasts Vanity Fair Over ‘Fake News’ On Jared Kushner’s Alleged Undisclosed Foreign Bank Accounts
articles.content_orig:
Jared Kushner is pushing back on a report involving a hacked iPhone, international spies and billion-dollar transfers from foreign governments.
An upcoming book by journalist Matthew Cole claims Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law, had access to more than $2 billion in "slush money funds" from Middle Eastern leaders in an attempt to influence U.S. foreign policy.
An excerpt of the book released Thursday details allegations encompassing Kushner's time as a senior White House adviser during the first Trump administration, which included a lead role in U.S. policy in the Middle East. Kushner had a major hand in negotiating key foreign policy deals that involved Israel, the Gulf states, China and Russia during that period.
Kushner and his legal team released fiery statements Thursday night categorically denying all accusations against him. Kushner said , "The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened." His attorney called them "false and defamatory" and said they intend to pursue legal action against those responsible, but did not specify whom.
The new book, "Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed's Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East," alleges Kushner had access to billions of dollars in undisclosed foreign bank accounts intended to pay for "influence within the U.S. government."
An excerpt from the book that was published in "Vanity Fair," but not independently verified by CBS News, says Dutch intelligence agents learned the Russians had hacked Kushner's iPhone in 2017 after flipping a Russian spy and subsequently gained access to Kushner's phone as well.
According to the report, "when Kushner used the phone, they could see his screen. Almost as soon as they got inside, the intelligence service began capturing every image of Kushner's screen as he used it."
At the time, Kushner served as a senior White House adviser to President Trump, including on Middle Eastern diplomacy.
The report alleges Dutch spies witnessed him log into a United Arab Emirates account that had allegedly received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan, and claims the leaders of Saudi Arabia and the UAE put at least $2 billion into multiple bank accounts linked to Kushner, including an account with Israel's Central Bank.
According to the book excerpt, the owners and managers of the accounts were often disguised as official government entities or charities, but the funds were actually intended for "off-the-books diplomatic objectives" such as striking a deal to end the Israeli-Palesteinian conflict.
The report also claims Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman put roughly $1 billion into at least one account for Kushner, citing a "person with knowledge of the money" saying "its allocation was for Kushner's personal benefit."
Kushner forcefully denied the accusations leveled in the "Vanity Fair" excerpt, writing in part, "The allegations made by this author are completely insane and never happened."
"We denied every claim on the record, yet the author provided not a single shred of verifiable evidence to substantiate them," he said.
"No bank statements, wire transfer records, account numbers, transaction dates, or other verifiable details were provided to support these extraordinary accusations," he said.
CBS News reached out to the White House, which referred us to a statement from Steven Cheung, who is assistant to the president and White House director of communications.
Cheung said the "bull**** Vanity Fair article comes from a book that is complete fiction, and was fabricated from the warped mind of failed spy thriller writer."
"He presents no evidence or even a shred of documentation. Just mysterious words from unnamed sources," Cheung said on X.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu vows West Bank military operation after attack kills two Israeli soldiers
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu vows West Bank military operation after attack kills two Israeli soldiers
articles.content_orig:
Diggers were seen demolishing Palestinian homes on Friday afternoon
The Israeli military has begun demolishing Palestinian buildings in the city of Hebron, after two Israeli soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military would "destroy" the neighbourhood where the two attackers came from, and that Israel was ready for "extensive action" in the occupied West Bank.
Three other soldiers were wounded in the attack at a checkpoint outside Hebron, before the gunmen were shot dead, officials say.
It comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel's general election taking place in four days' time.
Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen. Other footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire.
Photos of one of the suspected attackers were shared by AFP news agency
The incident has already begun to influence the ongoing election campaign, with Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - saying that his Likud party would cancel campaign events which had been set for Friday morning.
Speaking later from the scene, Netanyahu said that the military would "demolish this place and completely transform it," referring to the Hebron neighbourhood where the attackers are said to have come from.
It is common for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment.
Netanyahu likened his plans to previous operations in West Bank refugee camps where residential buildings were demolished and thousands were displaced.
He also said he had reviewed plans for the largest military operation in the West Bank in decades - though did not say when it could be carried out.
He added that he had imposed cordons around the city of Hebron - which has around 200,000 residents - and the nearby city of Halhul.
Netanyahu's far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for Israel to launch a campaign in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza or Lebanon," while far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to dismantle the Palestinian Authority.
On Thursday, Foreign Minister Israel Katz accused opposition leaders of undermining the government by criticising Netanyahu's warnings of an attack ahead of the election, saying they would be "responsible" for any future attack on the country.
Opposition chiefs, including frontrunner Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, offered their condolences to the families of the killed troops and praised those who killed the attackers.
The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.
At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.
Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says - not including those killed in Friday's attack.
