articles.title_orig: CoreWeave Is Down 13% in a Week. Here's the Price at Which I'd Buy
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave Is Down 13% in a Week. Here's the Price at Which I'd Buy
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave 's ( CRWV -2.46% ) stock has plunged 54% over the past 12 months, and it set a new 52-week low of $53.50 on Oct. 22. In the past week alone, it sank about 13%. Let's see why this neocloud stock fizzled out -- and if it's becoming a compelling buy at these prices.
CoreWeave was once an Ethereum miner, but it repurposed its Nvidia ( NVDA -0.59% ) GPUs to train AI models after the cryptocurrency market crashed in 2018.
Image source: Getty Images.
Today, CoreWeave operates 51 data centers that run over a quarter million Nvidia GPUs to remotely process AI tasks. That streamlined approach enables it to process advanced AI workloads roughly 35 times faster and at 80% lower cost than larger cloud platforms. Its largest customers include Meta Platforms , Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic. Nvidia also owns about 9% of CoreWeave, making it the company's top institutional investor.
CoreWeave went public last March. In 2025, its revenue soared 168% to $5.1 billion, and its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) rose 154% to $3.1 billion. Those explosive growth rates -- driven by the AI market 's breakneck expansion -- dazzled investors, and the stock surged from its IPO price of $40 per share to a record high of $183.58 per share on June 20, 2025.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/23/26
At its peak, CoreWeave's enterprise value hit $91.1 billion -- or 18 times the revenue it would generate in 2025. However, it struggled to maintain that premium valuation because investors were concerned about its steep losses and persistent dilution.
Even though its adjusted EBITDA was positive, it posted a net loss of $1.2 billion in 2025. That massive gap was driven by interest payments, equipment depreciation, lease and acquisition costs, and stock-based compensation, all of which were excluded from its adjusted EBITDA.
To stabilize its liquidity, CoreWeave issued more shares and convertible debt. That's why its share count has risen 28% since its IPO, and why it ended its latest quarter with $72 billion in total liabilities and a jaw-dropping debt-to-equity ratio of 14.3. Those glaring weaknesses suggested its business model wasn't sustainable yet, and the Fed's rate hike in September -- its first in three years -- made its messy balance sheet even less attractive.
By the end of the second quarter of 2026, CoreWeave's contracted revenue backlog had grown 246% year over year to $104 billion. For the full year, analysts expect its revenue and adjusted EBITDA to surge 151% to $12.9 billion, with adjusted EBITDA growing 144% to $7.6 billion. But on a GAAP basis, they expect its net loss to widen from $1.2 billion to $2.9 billion.
While CoreWeave's business is booming, it had only 1.85 GW of capacity at the end of June, compared to a contracted backlog of 4.2 GW. It expects to lease more data centers and buy more GPUs to narrow that gap next year, but that expansion will be costly.
For 2027, analysts expect its revenue to grow 106% to $26.5 billion, its adjusted EBITDA to grow 121% to $16.7 billion, and its net loss to narrow slightly to $2.8 billion. At its current enterprise value of $76.2 billion, it trades at just four times next year's sales and six times its adjusted EBITDA. Those low valuations should limit its downside potential, even if near-term concerns about rising rates and steep net losses weigh on its stock.
CoreWeave clearly has a first-mover advantage in the neocloud space ; it's firmly backed by Nvidia, and economies of scale should kick in as its business matures. I didn't love the stock when it skyrocketed after its IPO, but I think it's worth accumulating in the mid-50s -- as long as you can tune out the near-term noise and focus on its long-term growth potential.

Now that the first folding iPhone has launched, we’ll find out quickly what can go wrong.
The iPhone Duo officially goes on sale today, but a few units already have broken screens. According to posts on Reddit about the affected units, the issue appears to be happening at a similar spot on all of them: Some kind of problem shows up on the inner screen along the hinge and a strange bright line (or lines) across the right side of the display.

Had my iPhone Duo for about six hours and had probably opened it fewer than 20 times.
I was showing it to a friend, and as I opened it, I felt something around the internal hinge, underneath the screen.
As I continued opening it, I heard an audible crack, and the screen broke right along the hinge.
There were no marks or damage on the inner screen’s surface or the external hinge to suggest anything had been caught or damaged.
The user said that the Apple Store replaced their phone with “a brand-new one on the spot.”
A post showing an image of another broken screen includes a video in a comment demonstrating yet another.
And a separate Reddit thread collected other pictures of affected Duos.
Apple didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

articles.title_orig: How Can I Hang On To My Digital Life?
articles.title_zh: How Can I Hang On To My Digital Life?
articles.content_orig:
12:36 PM EDT on October 23, 2026
I've been watching the "available storage" bars on my various digital storage systems creep up over the last couple years, with a growing sense of dread. Each percentage point is a tick closer to an upgrade to my package—money I'll have to pay Apple, Google, and Dropbox to continue to store my digital life. Maybe more importantly, I'm aware of just how much stuff I produce every day, and as the mess grows, I wonder if I should do something about it. On worse days, I think maybe I should just succumb to the digital hoarder house I've built for myself.
It is probably my obsession with my own death, paired with the ever-present anxiety about whether the way I spend my days truly matters at all, that has led to an interest in personal archiving practices. My life's work amounts to several terabytes' worth of mp3s, wavs, text files, and jpegs that live on server space I pay to lease somewhere in the world. I like the idea of my work being accessible after I'm gone, and for a long time I trusted the infrastructure of the internet to do that archival work for me. But if the last 20 years have taught us anything, it's that only dummies blindly trust big tech to operate in their best interest.
"People do not realize how fragile digital media is," said Margot Note, an archivist who specializes in helping individuals and businesses create their own archives. Note told me about bit rot, which is a phenomenon where digital files become corrupted over time from neglect. To get specific: If left alone for too long, the individual bits that make up a digital file can unintentionally flip from 0 to 1 and vice versa, which eventually renders the file unreadable. "Digital files actually require active maintenance. And it's not something that you have to do right away, but over time, they're going to be unreadable." Note suggests to maintain files using two techniques: refreshing and migration. Refreshing refers to routinely moving data from one storage medium to a newer one, like taking a document from a floppy disk and saving it to a newer hard drive.
But there are other, more general concerns about the longevity of digital files. "I don't know if Microsoft Word is going to be around 100 years from now," she said. "You're dependent on the software. You're dependent on the hardware, and you're dependent on corporations that could go out of business. So if you put something in the cloud, you could lose access to it." Migration refers to updating data that was created for obsolete mediums or software into more modern forms, like converting a WordPerfect document to an updated version of Microsoft Word.
Because my specific flavor of neurosis blended with the knowledge that I'm soon going to give birth to a human, I was finally convinced to download Note's book, Creating Family Archives . What I found there was both useful and anxiety-inducing.
"External hard drives, if stored correctly and used sparingly, might last a decade," Note writes. "If not treated well, they may have five years of useful storage life." I thought about my stack of external hard drives sitting in an office drawer, some of which date back to 2010 and which haven't been connected to a computer in at least 10 years. I wasn't sure what kinds of files I would find in these old drives, but I hoped that my current MacBook could open the files that were created on a 2008 Dell laptop.
Note refers to the 3-2-1 rule of archiving: Make three copies of something, store it in at least two types of media, and keep one copy at a physically separate location. A practical example: You might keep an album of family photos on your phone, but also consider printing them out (for a second form of media), and storing digital versions on both an external hard drive and in cloud storage (which actually makes four copies, including the printed versions, in at least two physical locations, if you think of the cloud as server space that exists somewhere else in the world).
Here's what I was working with: 58 GB in my personal paid Google Drive, 6 GB in my Defector Google Drive, 3.19 TB in my personal paid Dropbox, 535.45 GB in my paid iCloud, and six external hard drives. The only small bright spot in my current archiving practice is that I store nothing on my computer; after going through enough computer catastrophes, I am religious about saving everything important directly to Dropbox. This gives me some peace, because I know I can switch devices at any point, but it also means my Dropbox is a mess.
Some of the goals I had for this project:
First, I dug out my 8TB hard drive and plugged it in. The last time I used it was in 2020, when I backed up my wedding photos. This was where I hit my first technological roadblock. The hard drive would need to be reformatted before I could add any new data to it, because it had previously been formatted for an older computer I no longer have. Without getting too into the weeds, the hard drive was meant for a PC system, and so each time it connected to a Mac, it had to be formatted specifically for that computer if I wanted to add or remove from it.
This meant that I actually had to delete everything on the hard drive before I could proceed, which would have been a nightmare if I had saved anything more to the hard drive, or had been relying on it as my sole archival source. Luckily, I still had my wedding photos on my Dropbox account, so I could reformat the drive without losing anything (3-2-1 already coming in clutch!). But I could see how this would have posed a much bigger problem if I'd had more stored on this hard drive and didn’t have a system set up to regularly migrate my files.
Once the hard drive was reformatted and writable, I created two folders on it: "family-archive" and "alex-archive." Within each of those folders, I created folders for each year starting in 2016, as well as a "pre-2016" folder for any loose ends that have survived longer than a decade. I followed the naming convention guidelines set out by Preserve This Podcast , which was an archiving project created by the Metropolitan New York Library Council. In order to increase the likelihood that my file names will be readable by future technologies, I kept them all lowercase and replaced spaces with dashes or underscores.
A useful piece of advice Note gave me was to start with my oldest files first. "Those are the most fragile, and then you're gonna forget what those things are as far as what you're looking at," she said.
So I decided to start with my personal Google Drive. I sorted it in chronological order and came face-to-face with 19-year-old me. The oldest document in my drive was from 2011, a writing sample for an internship I ended up getting. There was absolutely nothing special about this piece of writing, which was just the text of an article I'd written for the student newspaper, but I was touched to see evidence of my first-ever professional application. I downloaded it and saved it to the pre-2016 folder. Then I deleted it from my Google Drive.
Another important thing Note reminded me was that you are in charge of your own archive. You are not beholden to the morass of stuff you have accumulated over the years. You can delete as much as you want and only archive what matters to you. This archive had two purposes for me: to preserve family photos, videos, and documents; and to preserve my work archive as much as possible. I long ago accepted that the majority of my blogs will probably end up lost to link rot on the internet, but I do want to keep a record of the things I’m most proud of making.
I went through the documents and found grocery lists and spreadsheets of job applications (deleted), but I also found my first awkward attempts at fiction and all the videos from a YouTube series I made about side hustles for a now-defunct feminist blog back in 2015. As I downloaded and saved files, I created new subfolders that started to follow a pattern for each year: There

articles.title_orig: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
articles.title_zh: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
articles.content_orig:
Gamers still hoping against hope for a true follow-up to Half-Life 2 (after so, so many years ) may remember last year’s flurry of speculation that Half-Life 3 was finally nearing completion . Amid all those rumors, though, we never got any official sign from anyone inside Valve that a Half-Life project was currently in development.
That changed this week thanks to an apparent slip-up during a panel at GameSoundCon , an industry conference devoted to “the art, technology, and business of game audio.” In a panel devoted to Valve’s use of open audio engines (captured in this Vimeo clip ), Valve composer and audio artist Mike Morasky let an interesting string of three letters slip while talking about the way the company implements high dynamic range (HDR) audio:
Our HDR system is basically that’s one of the three pieces that come together to make an HDR that you can easily optimize. And in fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version , so on and so forth [emphasis added].
“HLX,” of course, has been widely reported as the internal code name for Valve’s next Half-Life project. The codename has shown up in Valve engine code since at least 2024 , but it has never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until now (though Morasky was responsible for a close call in an interview last year).
In the panel video, fellow panelist and Valve sound designer David Feise can be seen mumbling a sarcastic “nice work” to Morasky after the HLX codename slips out of his mouth. Later, while the audience is clapping at the end of the Q&A session, Feise leans in to Morasky and appears to say, “Good job—you only said HLX once!”
An official utterance of the “HLX” shibboleth is of course a good sign for those looking for any indication of the franchise continuing beyond 2020’s Half-Life Alyx . But the question of when Valve will make its next Half-Life project official still looms large.
Remember, it was just under a year ago that journalist Mike Straw was adamant that Half-Life 3 would be a Steam Machine launch title . Now that the Steam Machine launch has come and gone without even a nod toward an announcement, we can understand why Valve watchers would be more gun-shy than usual over any new rumors.
Longtime Valve watcher Tyler McVicker—who said Half-Life 3 was in the “final stages of development” and suggested a 2026 announcement was “likely” last year—admitted in a recent video that he now doesn’t believe that HLX is being announced this calendar year. But he also pointed to recently increased coding activity within Valve (as measured by externally viewable internal “commit” numbers) that something big might be coming sooner than later.
One thing is for sure: Whenever Half-Life 3 finally is announced and released, it will have to be truly incredible to make up for the loss of the long-running metagame of speculating about its mere existence .

articles.title_zh: Nvidia Stock’s 2 Critical Flaws and More Reasons an Analyst Says Sell
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
NVDA's CUDA ecosystem locks in developers and clouds with every chip generation, while Q2 revenue surged 106% to $96B with next-quarter guidance of $108B.
AMD trades at a steep P/E of 191 with 50% gross margins and declining free cash flow, while Broadcom's 221% AI revenue growth comes with heavy debt and customer concentration risk.
Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)
I have bought NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) on dip after dip, and this latest slide put the stock back at the top of my research list. Shares fell 4.4% in the most recent session and 7.28% over the past month, closing at $212.21. That pullback stands out given NVIDIA's position in AI computing.
My thesis comes down to one point. AI models run on NVIDIA, and the CUDA software layer makes leaving expensive. On the August call, CEO Jensen Huang said "Our position in open models is very good because the CUDA ecosystem is literally everywhere." Developers write for CUDA, clouds rent CUDA, and each new chip generation inherits that installed base. That lock-in strengthens with each chip generation.
First, growth at scale. Revenue for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 reached $96.22B, up 105.8% year over year. Data Center revenue hit $89.02B, up 117%, and networking grew 138%. That tells me customers buy the whole AI factory, chips and connections together. Guidance calls for $108.0B ±2% next quarter.
Second, profitability. NVIDIA runs a 71.07% gross margin, a 60.38% operating margin, and a 101.49% return on equity. Fiscal 2026 free cash flow came in at $96.58B.
The balance sheet and capital return also look strong. Its debt-to-equity stands at 0.073, and interest coverage at 503.42x. NVIDIA returned about $26.0B in Q2 and holds $99.0B of remaining buyback authorization. The 0.019% yield pays me little, so I own this for compounding, and a P/E of 43 looks reasonable for that growth rate.

Advanced Micro Devices ( NASDAQ:AMD ) grew Data Center revenue 107% last quarter. Still, it trades at a P/E of 191, with a gross margin near 49.5%, and its Q2 free cash flow fell 9.89%. AMD itself lists ROCm's competition with established developer ecosystems as a risk.
Broadcom ( NASDAQ:AVGO ) posted AI semiconductor revenue of $16.70 billion, up 221%. Its own filings flag dependence on a limited number of AI customers and significant indebtedness. I prefer NVIDIA's near-debt-free platform.
Supply commitments rose to $279.0B from $119.0B one quarter earlier, mostly linked to Vera Rubin memory. Days sales outstanding extended to 60 days from 45, and guidance excludes China Data Center compute. If AI spending stalls, those commitments could hurt margins and cash flow.
Demand still exceeds supply. Huang said "Even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%." NVIDIA holds Vera Rubin purchase orders from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud and system OEM. Those orders make the commitments look like preparation to me.
NVIDIA's revenue opportunity per gigawatt rises to $40 billion with Vera Rubin from $25 billion with Blackwell. Top hyperscaler capex should reach nearly $800 billion in 2026 and $1.3 trillion in 2027. The stock has returned 837.87% over five years, and my long-term view remains the same. articles.title_orig: Leaked trove reveals extent of far-right AfD’s efforts to court Trump and Maga allies
articles.title_zh: Leaked trove reveals extent of far-right AfD’s efforts to court Trump and Maga allies
articles.content_orig:
Exclusive: Documents show German party’s scramble to request support after president’s 2016 election win and co-leader’s pursuit of Steve Bannon
A data leak from Germany’s far-right German Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) has revealed the extent of efforts by the party to court Donald Trump and other leading figures in the Maga movement, stretching back more than a decade.
The trove reveals the pains the AfD took in wooing the president, whom they saw from the beginning as a potential ally, with senior party officials agonising over the wording of an obsequious congratulatory telegram when he was elected in 2016, which included the wish that his “hopes as a person be fulfilled”.
The AfD became a home for anti-immigration voters after 1.2 million refugees arrived in Germany in 2015 and 2016. It entered the Bundestag, Germany’s parliament, in 2017 with 12.6% of the vote , came second in the February 2025 federal election with 20.8% , and now leads national polls at about 30% . In September it won 43.8% of the vote in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, and it is now trying to form Germany’s first far-right state government since the second world war.
Trump hailed the win in Saxony-Anhalt in a post on his Truth Social, concluding his message with a German version of his Make America Great Again acronym, “MGGA!!!”
Germany’s domestic intelligence agency monitors the party as a suspected rightwing extremist organisation , and state agencies classify five of its regional branches as confirmed extremist .
Its leader in the central Thuringia region, Björn Höcke, was convicted in 2024 of knowingly using a slogan of the SA, the Nazi party’s paramilitary wing. AfD politicians also attended a meeting with extremists at which a mass-deportation “masterplan” was discussed. Its 2025 election programme calls for lifting sanctions on Russia and repairing the Nord Stream gas pipelines programme . Nearly all of Germany’s other parties have kept a “firewall”, refusing to govern with it.
Media outlets including the Guardian have reported on the apparently friendly contacts between the party and the US state department during Trump’s second term.
The leaked documents show AfD officials quickly moving to requests for support from the White House on policy issues when he first won the 2016 election.
Others show a burgeoning political courtship between senior figures including the AfD’s now leader, Alice Weidel, and the key Trump ideologue Steve Bannon.
The data, provided to reporters by the transparency organisation Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), covers more than 420,000 emails, along with documents and personnel records, from the party’s foundation in 2013 to the present, with most coming before 2019.
The AfD said in a statement on Monday that a hosting provider used by the party had been attacked at the end of September and that “only a few mailboxes” had been copied. It told the news agency dpa that most of those mailboxes had not been used for years, and party sources were quoted as saying the published material appeared to be authentic.
AfD figures praised Trump ahead of his first election in 2016, with then leader Frauke Petry calling him a “refreshingly alternative proposition” in the spring of 2016. On the day after Trump won the presidency, Petry said the victory was “encouraging for Germany and for Europe” .
The hacked documents reveal that in the wake of his election, the party scrambled to send an ingratiating telegram to the new president.
Mainstream German politicians greeted Trump’s election with skepticism. On 9 November 2016, the then chancellor, Angela Merkel, offered Trump “close cooperation” only “on the basis of … values” including respect for human dignity “regardless of origin, skin colour, religion, gender, sexual orientation or political views”. The then defence minister, Ursula von der Leyen, called the result a “ huge shock ”. The next day the vice-chancellor, Sigmar Gabriel, reportedly called Trump the “forerunner of a new authoritarian and chauvinist international”, and he counted the AfD among its forces.
On 10 November, Petry emailed the party’s federal board proposing “an official and brief congratulatory telegram to the future US president”. German politics, she wrote, was “once again outdoing itself in politically unacceptable behaviour”; the AfD was “already perceived as the ones who don’t join in the majority howl of the political establishment” and, “as the only German party welcoming a new beginning in the US”, should say so officially.
Eleven of the board’s 13 members replied, all in favour. Current leader Weidel wrote “Yes:-)”. Beatrix von Storch, now deputy leader of the party’s Bundestag group, wrote: “Couldn’t be more of a yes.”
Board member Dirk Driesang added that Trump should also receive, “by post (?)”, the party’s manifesto in English.
The telegram went out on 11 November under Petry’s name, “on behalf of the federal board”, and was released to the press. It told the president-elect: “We are confident that you will readjust the transatlantic relationship and end the wars in Syria and Ukraine by mutual agreement with Russia.”
A second message, for the inauguration, was planned more carefully, and included a concrete request for a political favor. On 11 January 2017, Driesang asked for it to be put on the agenda of the board’s next conference call, “this time faster and better prepared”, and proposed adding a request: “Please support us in our efforts to remove the enemy-state clause from the UN charter.”
The “enemy state” clauses were written into the UN charter in 1945, and exempted action against “any state which during the second world war has been an enemy of any signatory” from the charter’s normal rules, so that the wartime allies could move against any “renewal of aggressive policy” by Germany, Japan or their allies. The general assembly declared them obsolete in 1995 and resolved to repeal them, but the text has never been amended, because changing the charter needs ratification by two-thirds of member states and all five permanent members of the security council.
No German party currently defends the clauses, but the Bundestag’s own research service wrote in 2017 that international lawyers unanimously regard the clauses as having no practical relevance . On the German right, however, the clauses are totemic , and viewed as a limitation on German sovereignty. The AfD’s Bundestag group demanded its deletion in a 2020 motion that called it a “relic of the past” which “indirectly designates Germany an ‘enemy state’”, and every other party voted it down .
AfD’s federal board adopted the enemy state request on its call of 16 January, according to the federal office’s record of the decision contained in the leaked documents.
When the office circulated an English draft on 19 January, Georg Pazderski, then the party’s Berlin leader and a member of its federal board, objected to the tone and to the request for support: “You don’t address the president as Mr Trump, he is Mr President. Otherwise a bit wordy and flowery. I stand by it: the enemy-state clause doesn’t belong in this letter at all. You don’t do that in a letter of congratulation. It looks like a begging letter.”
Driesang replied at 6.16 the next morning: “Personally I of course find the style appropriate, otherwise I wouldn’t have written it that way.”
The office also wanted to know how the telegram should reach Trump: “directly to Trump’s campaign team … or through official diplomatic channels (e.g. the US embassy in Berlin)?”
André Poggenburg, then the party’s leader in Saxony-Anhalt, answered: “all available channels.”
The text released on the afternoon of 20 January, signed by Petry and her then co-leader Jörg Meuthen, kept the request. It told Trump that the clause stood in Germany’s way “as a strange anachronism”, and asked him to see the AfD “as natural allies at your side, because we are the only German party in clear opposition to the wrong pol

Brent crude nears $120 as escalating Saudi-Houthi tensions fuel another weekly oil price rally, putting fresh pressure on Trump.
The slow creep of oil prices towards the $120 per barrel mark is a nightmarish scenario for US President Trump, even though there has been little fundamental change in the crude oil markets. A slight drop in freight rates and a ubiquitous flattening of backwardated curves lowered differentials of most grades globally, offsetting some of the pressures coming from higher crude benchmarks. Be that as it may, an escalating Saudi-Houthi conflict paved the way for another 4% weekly gain, with ICE Brent trading around $117 per barrel.
First Russian Diesel Cargo Heads for New York. A non-sanctioned tanker, the Maltese-flagged Agioi Fanendes, left Russia’s Baltic Sea port of Primorsk with New York listed as its destination , marking the first diesel cargo under Trump’s deal with Moscow with final delivery expected on November 7.
Libya Oil Output Falls After Protests Reemerge. Libya's NOC said unauthorized individuals shut a pipeline valve serving the Hamada and Tahara fields, cutting output by 50,000 and 40,000 b/d respectively, as recurring protests jeopardize crude production that provides 90% of state revenues.
Europe Enters Winter with Gas at Four-Year Highs. Europe’s TTF gas benchmark rose above €93/MWh ($30 per MMBtu), the highest since December 2022, as restricted Qatari LNG supply coincided with colder weather and storage peaking below 75%, leaving Europe highly exposed ahead of winter.
Aramco Evacuates HQ After Houthi Attacks. Saudi Aramco (TADAWUL:2222) ordered staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and temporarily work from home after the HQ was attacked by the Houthis, the first such move since the Iran war began, with drone strikes also killing two at the Shaybah oilfield.
Qatar Looks to Rebuild Its LNG Supply Base. QatarEnergy is seeking additional long-term cargoes from the US and potentially Asia after securing its first agreement with US developer Cheniere (NYSE:LNG), locking in 4 million tonnes of LNG per year until 2054, as domestic LNG outflows remain constrained.
Trump Taps Emergency Diesel Stockpiles. The US Energy Department is offering 315,000 barrels of diesel, one-third of its Northeast reserve, to ease regional disruptions as global diesel exports decline, while portraying the loan as temporary relief, with first Russian cargoes arriving in early November.
Japan Weighs Phasing Out Gasoline Subsidies. The Japanese government is considering phasing down gasoline subsidies from December as the program costs billions monthly, rapidly depleting a $20 billion budget, with average prices potentially rising from $4.1 per gallon now to $4.35 per gallon in January.
Trump Sees Wind Turbines as a Security Threat. US President Trump declared imported wind turbines and components a national security threat over cybersecurity and foreign dependence concerns, citing a Commerce Department investigation, ordering trade officials to discuss the issue with trading partners.
Indonesia Considers Halting Gas Exports. Indonesia may halt pipeline gas exports to neighbouring countries as Jakarta seeks to prioritize rising domestic demand, potentially a great blow to Singapore as such a move would remove some 7 bcm of supply, equivalent to 45% of the city-state’s consumption.
Mexico Doubles Down on Oil Exploration. Mexico’s state oil company Pemex pledged to direct $99 billion towards its upstream business in 2025-2030, 80% of its entire investment budget, seeking to counter declining production as crude oil output hovers at a meagre 1.34 million b/d in 2026 to date.
Kashagan Arbitration Court Rejects $12bn Cost Claims. The Permanent Court of Arbitration in the Hague rejected the Kazakh government’s $12 billion cost claims against international oil majors operating the giant Kashagan field, claiming it is too late to claim costs incurred between 2011 and 2015.
EU Starts Work on 22 nd Russia Sanctions Package. The EU's draft 22nd sanctions package would add 12 individuals and 105 entities tied to Russian oil production, trading, refining, shipping and logistics, doubling down on pressure as Washington and Moscow discuss broader bilateral economic issues.
UAE Oil Spill Threatens Civilian Infrastructure. UAE a uthorities closed coastal areas around Umm Al Quwain and launched containment operations after a tanker—the Gem No.2 VLCC struck by missiles two weeks ago—began leaking oil, with currents carrying contamination towards desalination plants.
Beijing Orders a Nationwide Oil Supply Boost. The Chinese government instructed state oil companies PetroChina, Sinopec and CNOOC to expedite oil exploration and production to shield the country from supply shocks, going beyond the 2% annual growth rate with current oil output at 4.43 million b/d.
America’s Gas Glut Defies the Global Rally. Henry Hub gas futures fell to a two-month low of $2.66 per MMBtu as mild weather, recovering offshore supply and above-average US inventories outweigh record LNG demand, with the calendar year 2027 futures falling to a 5-year low of $3.09 per MMBtu.

articles.title_orig: 'We're Victims of Xbox's Change in Strategy': Dishonored Dev Has Weeks to Save Itself
articles.title_zh: 'We're Victims of Xbox's Change in Strategy': Dishonored Dev Has Weeks to Save Itself
articles.content_orig:
Update [ Fri 23rd Oct 2026, 5:30pm ]:
While the future of Arkane Lyon seemed precarious following today’s updates, Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier has followed up with more positive news.
He says there are “multiple paths being explored” to save the studio and he’d “be surprised if it is shut down”.
He does warn, however, that “anything can happen during negotiations”.
Original Story: While the future of former Xbox first-party devs like Double Fine and Undead Labs has already been determined, it’s been a while since we heard word from Arkane Lyon , the studio behind the acclaimed Dishonored games.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
Now an article by Le Monde (paywalled) gives an insight into the struggles of the French studio, as it races to find a buyer before a 13th November deadline.
As you may recall, Microsoft was unable to close the studio immediately due to a consultation period demanded by French law. The Redmond firm is obligated to try to sell the studio, but a mandated three month deadline is now coming to a close.
The team has until 13th November to find new funding, otherwise the studio will be shuttered and around 217 jobs will be lost. According to the report, negotiations are ongoing.
Union representatives claim the team’s current project, Marvel’s Blade – which was announced in 2023 – is “nearing the end of production”. Spokespeople for the studio believe it will be a success if it sees the light of day.
But those same people blame Microsoft for its “disrespectful” treatment of the team.
“We are collateral victims of Xbox’s change in strategy,” one of the people said.
As alluded to above, Microsoft has already shuttered UK studio Ninja Theory , and offloaded various other teams like Compulsion Games et al.
It’s also in the process of reorganising its entire first-party operations, seemingly sunsetting Xbox Game Studios as it places its remaining teams under the umbrella of Bethesda and Activision. Its objective is to focus on big franchises like Fallout and Call of Duty .
The scary part is that the platform holder is not done yet: it’s cut over 1,800 jobs so far, but more redundancies are coming , as it aims to eliminate 3,200 roles overall.

articles.title_orig: Melania Trump helps forge a ceasefire deal in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city, White House says
articles.title_zh: Melania Trump helps forge a ceasefire deal in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city, White House says
articles.content_orig:
US First Lady Melania Trump has "successfully secured" a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, the White House has said.
It said the truce in the "front-line war city on the brink of disaster" without medicine, food and clean water would begin on 29 October.
Ukraine and Russia confirmed the deal was agreed to evacuate residents and deliver aid. Moscow said its forces would stop firing at 04:00 (02:00 GMT) on 27 October.
Oleshky was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Trapped between Ukrainian positions across the Dnipro River and Russian forces to the east, residents have recently resorted to eating garden weeds to survive.
The White House statement said Melania Trump and one of her representatives had worked "directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localised ceasefire".
"Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require," she is quoted as saying.
"Residents who wish to evacuate will receive co-ordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine."
Melania Trump added that Oleshky residents "have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks" and that "without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible".
The statement did not say how long the ceasefire would be in place for.
Davyd Arakhamia, a Ukrainian MP who heads President Volodymyr Zelensky's party in parliament, later said "an operation to unblock the settlement of Oleshky and its surroundings will begin in the near future".
"To achieve this goal, a ceasefire will be achieved in the near future, as announced by the First Lady of the United States, Melania Trump," he said. No date or time has been announced by Kyiv yet.
In Russia, President Vladimir Putin's spokesman confirmed that, "those who wish to do so will be able to leave this settlement".
Last month, some of the remaining Oleshky residents told the BBC harrowing accounts of how they were surviving in the city that was being constantly shelled and cut off from food and water.
They said that children remaining in wider Oleshky were suffering from malnutrition, a lack of medical services and were "degrading" without access to education.
Many also told the BBC there was only one hospital partially operational, opening a few days a week to perform critical amputations.
The local population was living under a "full blockade" by Russian forces, according to Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.
Ukraine says it has attempted to deliver supplies to the area but has not had success in recent months.
The Kremlin in September acknowledged that Oleshky was facing "a critical situation" and "problems with supplies of food and medicine", but added that "Russia's military was working to resolve them" and blamed Kyiv.
Oleshky was home to 24,000 people before Russia's full-scale invasion. Now  Ukraine estimates that some 6,000 people remain in the city and its surrounding areas, including 200 children.
It is also one of a number of settlements where thousands of people lost their homes to a massive flooding caused by the collapse of Nova Khakovka Dam in 2023. Ukraine and its allies accused Russia of blowing up the dam, while Russia blamed Ukraine.
While the US first lady is relatively lower profile than some of her predecessors - and only occasionally seen at White House events - she has become involved in addressing humanitarian issues stemming from the Russia-Ukraine war.
In August 2025, Melania Trump penned a letter to Putin, telling him it was "time to protect children and future generations worldwide".
Although she did not mention Ukraine by name, just days later at the White House Zelensky handed over a letter from his wife Olena, thanking her for her efforts on children.
In a rare public appearance in October the same year, the US first lady said that Putin had answered directly in writing and that her representatives were working with the Russian president's team to repatriate Ukrainian children from Russia and vice versa.
Some 34 children have reportedly been returned since 2025, including five this July.
According to US President Donald Trump, his wife has also privately expressed scepticism about Putin and his desire to achieve peace.
"I'd get home, I'd say, 'First lady, I had the most wonderful talk with Vladimir. I think we're finished'," Trump said in July last year.
"And then I'll turn on the television, or she'll say to me one time, 'Wow, that's strange because they just bombed a nursing home.'"

articles.title_orig: SpaceX wants to be America's fourth phone carrier — tower owners are cashing in
articles.title_zh: SpaceX wants to be America's fourth phone carrier — tower owners are cashing in
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Elon Musk's SpaceX doesn't just want to beam the internet from space. It wants to sell you a phone plan, and the companies that own the cell towers are already cashing in.
SpaceX ( SPCX ) is in talks for access to at least 80,000 US cell sites, Bloomberg reported Thursday , a step toward building a fourth nationwide carrier .
Crown Castle ( CCI ) is up double digits Friday, with American Tower ( AMT ) and SBA Communications ( SBAC ) close behind. AT&T ( T ) and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) are sliding, and Verizon ( VZ ) is lower too.
The biggest tile on that map is SpaceX itself. At about $2 trillion, it's worth roughly three times all six phone and tower companies combined, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
It's the second time this month the two groups have split this hard. On Oct. 9, SpaceX agreed to pay about $8 billion for a nationwide block of wireless airwaves. Tower stocks jumped, and the carriers sank by double digits that day. Since then, Crown Castle is up 27%, and AT&T is down 14%.
Eighty thousand sites is a big ask. That's about half of the 158,500 cell towers in the US, according to the Wireless Infrastructure Association. American Tower has about 41,000 sites in the US and Canada, and Crown Castle about 40,000.
AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile bring in about 85% of American Tower's US and Canada revenue. For the tower owners, SpaceX would be a new tenant. For the carriers, it would be a new rival.
The market is pricing that in. The carriers have shed about $21 billion in market value Friday, while the tower stocks have added about $9 billion.
Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant didn't name names on Wednesday's earnings call, but he left the door open. "You can assume that we're talking to all parties," he said.
Nothing is signed yet. The talks are still far from a formal lease deal, and some see them as a bargaining chip in SpaceX's dealings with the carriers. Better satellites could also mean SpaceX needs fewer towers than it's asking for.
The next test comes Tuesday, when American Tower reports earnings. Watch whether management talks up SpaceX as a customer, or whether the rally starts to cool.

articles.title_orig: American Airlines says airfares could stay elevated even if fuel prices drop
articles.title_zh: American Airlines says airfares could stay elevated even if fuel prices drop
articles.content_orig:
Gen Z travelers are cutting back on dining, haircuts and everyday expenses to afford trips as homeownership and other traditional milestones feel increasingly out of reach.
American Airlines issued a warning that airfares are likely to remain elevated even if there's a decline in oil prices after losses the carrier suffered earlier in the year amid surging fuel costs.
The carrier's CFO, Devon May, told the Financial Times that "if fuel comes down, I think airfares probably stay largely where they're at right now."
"If fuel prices go up, we need to generate higher yield, we need to generate higher fares to offset that higher fuel price," May said.
American Airlines on Thursday released its earnings for the third quarter, reporting deeper losses in 2026 and updating its forecast to reflect anticipated losses between $1 and $1.60 a share on an adjusted basis this year. Its July forecast ranged from a loss of 65 cents and a profit of 65 cents.
MAJOR AIRLINES CUT FLIGHTS AS HIGHER JET FUEL PRICES HIT CARRIERS
American Airlines projected deeper losses in 2026 due to the surge in fuel costs. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
May told the FT that airlines' ticket prices hadn't fully recovered in real terms since the disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic , saying that the price hikes "ideally should have happened back in 2024, but the industry found itself in an oversupply environment."
"This was the first year that everything came together in a way that we were able to push yields back up to where they were seven years ago in real terms," May told the outlet.
AMERICAN AIRLINES ADDS $1,000 TRUMP ACCOUNT MATCH FOR WORKERS' CHILDREN
American Airlines said it expects higher fuel costs to persist into the fourth quarter. (Daniel Slim/AFP via Getty Images)
The company reported a 19% year-over-year increase in third quarter revenue , which was above the high end of its previous guidance range and was the highest in company history when excluding the years following the pandemic.
However, fuel expenses in the third quarter surged 67.5% compared with the same period a year ago, which translated to $1.9 billion in higher fuel costs based on an average price of $3.85 a gallon.
American also forecast higher fuel prices will continue into the company's fourth quarter, with the carrier expecting to face an average fuel price of about $4.70 a gallon – a figure that would nearly double the price in the fourth quarter of 2025 and increase fuel expenses by $2.8 billion year over year.
AMERICAN AIRLINES BETS BIG ON INTERNATIONAL FLIGHTS WITH 7 NEW ROUTES
Due to the elevated fuel prices , American said that it expects its network growth to slow in 2027 when compared with 2026 levels.
Higher fuel prices have caused airfares to surge, with the most recent data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics showing that airline fares were up 22.4% compared with a year ago in September.

articles.title_orig: Commission weighs best strategy for new trade talks with China
articles.title_zh: Commission weighs best strategy for new trade talks with China
articles.content_orig:
EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič said on Friday that the EU was walking a tightrope in negotiations with Beijing, weighing conventional trade measures against broader political considerations.
After several months of negotiations, Brussels and Beijing reached a deal on 9 October to curb imports of hybrid cars from China. However, the agreement is unlikely to significantly narrow the EU’s record trade deficit with China, which has reached €1 billion a day, a gap the European Commission is seeking to reduce.
“There are whole sectors under threat; each head of states and government is concerned that there might be potential heavy losses of the jobs,” Šefčovič said on Friday, after a meeting of the 27 trade ministers in Ireland.
He added: “We have to proceed not only with the traditional trade techniques, but also with a very political approach, how to balance the trade between between China and the European Union.”
A new round of discussions is taking place at a technical level with Beijing until the end of the year, with political negotiation scheduled for January and March 2027.
But given the urgency, EU leaders gave the European Commission a political mandate last week to work on a “kill switch” tool that would allow Europeans to cut off China's access to their market to counter economic distortions.
Under the October deal, the EU will introduce country-specific quotas allowing 350,000 Chinese hybrid cars onto the European market annually over four years, with a fixed annual adjustment rate of 6%.
The Commission aims to extend the agreement to other sectors, but EU officials warn that progress will also depend on Beijing’s response to the EU executive’s efforts to strengthen its trade defence tools.
The Commission is set to present a new instrument on 9 October aimed at encouraging EU companies to diversify their suppliers of strategic products to reduce their dependence on China.
It also hopes to present a proposal for the so-called “kill switch” that same week and ahead of the December summit of EU leaders. Pushed by France and Germany earlier this month, it would allow the Commission to adopt radical measures against Beijing in the event of economic pressure on the EU market.
Another unilateral EU trade defence measure targeting Chinese chemicals and industrial machinery could also come in December, with the risk of prompting Chinese countermeasures.
According to the latest Chinese customs data, China's exports to the EU have continued to surge, rising by 25% over the past year.

Anthropic’s public listing, which is expected this year at a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, is bound to be a windfall for both early-stage and later-stage investors. Here is what some backers in the leading AI lab are worth at that last round’s price, according to Bloomberg :
Eric Schmidt: The former Google CEO invested in Anthropic’s Series A in 2021, when the startup was valued at $461 million, according to PitchBook data. Today, Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, and even at its current private valuation, his stake is worth nearly $10 billion.

Sequoia: The famed VC firm backed the AI lab for the first time only earlier this year, when the company was already valued at $380 billion. The $3 billion investment gave it about 1% ownership, which means it has already more than doubled its investment.
Sound Ventures: The firm, launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, invested $35 million in Anthropic’s 2023 Series C round and has since funneled an additional $400 million into the company, resulting in a stake that’s worth billions now. Spark Capital: The only VC firm known to hold a board seat at Anthropic invested $75 million in that same 2023 Series C round, when it was valued at $5 billion. That position has ballooned more than ninetyfold to $7 billion.

articles.title_orig: Nearly 12 Million Capcom ID Accounts Affected in Huge Data Breach
articles.title_zh: Nearly 12 Million Capcom ID Accounts Affected in Huge Data Breach
articles.content_orig:
Capcom has been hit by a data breach that affected over 11.7 million Capcom ID accounts.
Capcom ID is used to manage online features, web services, and multiplayer across its portfolio, including for titles such as Street Fighter 6, Monster Hunter, and Resident Evil.
The publisher determined that on October 19, customer information was accessed by an unauthorised third party.
"Capcom has not confirmed any compromise of Capcom ID account login passwords originally set by customers themselves," the publisher said in a statement posted yesterday.
"However, Capcom has confirmed that passwords were changed without authorisation on 196 accounts. The passwords associated with these accounts have already been reset, and the company continues to investigate the scope of any impact resulting from this incident."
"Capcom has completed emergency response measures and has identified and addressed the attack method involved in this incident. Services that use Capcom ID, including games, remain available. Going forward, the company will begin contacting affected customers and has established dedicated customer-support channels for inquiries regarding this matter."
In an update posted today (October 23), Capcom said it had "confirmed that login passwords had been changed without authorisation for 196 accounts due to this incident. During the subsequent investigation, the company has determined the scope of impact stemming from the unauthorised change of passwords."
The publisher determined that this third party accessed the e-Capcom (online store operated by Capcom in Japan) account pages of 19 of the 196 accounts whose passwords had been changed.
Affected information included: name, name in Japanese phonetic characters, telephone number, postal code, address, gender, date of birth, purchase history, e-Capcom customer inquiry history, and saved address book information.
Credit card information was not affected.
"The investigation into the scope of the impact from this incident has been completed. Capcom will nevertheless continue monitoring Capcom ID and related services. The Company takes this incident extremely seriously and will steadily implement measures to prevent recurrence while working to further strengthen its information-security framework."
Capcom was previously hit by a ransomware attack in November 2020 that compromised the data of 16,415 people.
The publisher said the maximum number of people potentially affected by the hack could be 390,000.

articles.title_orig: Many feared trapped as a tall building collapses in Kenya
articles.title_zh: Many feared trapped as a tall building collapses in Kenya
articles.content_orig:
Many people are feared to be trapped in Kenya’s capital, Nairobi, after a multistorey building under construction collapsed, leaving a huge mound of concrete as rescuers dig through the rubble.
The building came down on Friday at about 1pm local time (10:00GMT) on a busy commercial street in Eastleigh, a neighbourhood crowded with thousands of traders and residents.
Nairobi police chief Issa Mohamud said more than 10 upper floors were under construction. The ground floor had been rented to an electronics shop, a butchery and a grocery, according to The Associated Press news agency.
Al Jazeera’s Catherine Soi, reporting from Nairobi, said the developers and authorities are being asked “to answer now” as people were not supposed to be inside a building under construction.
She said rescue efforts were expected to continue through Friday night and Saturday.
Rescuers used poles stripped from trees and excavators to move concrete bound with steel, as heavy equipment was slow to arrive.
Mohamud said one injured woman had been rescued and taken to hospital, while another person who had been calling for help had gone silent. He warned of a potential second collapse because the building was leaning on its neighbour.
Local media reported looting immediately after the collapse and police firing tear gas to disperse crowds.
Joseph Kaula, a plasterer working on the fifth floor of the collapsed building, told AP that he was the last person to walk out.
“The whole area was filled with dust,” he said.
Relatives of those trapped said some had phoned for help immediately after the collapse, but their phones later became unreachable. A tent was set up to report missing relatives.
“Our concern is to save lives,” Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja told reporters.
He said the building had been approved for construction but had no certificate of occupation, so opening shops on the ground floor was illegal.
“This has potentially cost lives,” he told reporters on site.
He said that it was possible “one or two” people had died and that more would be known as time went on.
Kenya’s National Building Inspectorate found that 87 percent of buildings audited nationwide last year failed to meet standards or lacked approvals, according to the AFP news agency.
Sakaja said county governments needed stronger enforcement powers, calling lenient penalties a “slap on the wrist”. Police said they would carry out investigations and anyone found negligent would face the law.

In contrast with the international benchmark futures prices, the prices of physical crudes from the Middle East have softened this week, as oil continues to flow out of the Persian Gulf in ship-to-ship transfers offshore Oman and producers offer competitive prices to Asian buyers.
Some crude grades from Iraq and Oman have sunk into deep discounts to the physical Dubai benchmark. Iraq’s Basrah Medium, for example, was recently sold at a discount of $10 per barrel to the Dubai benchmark, compared to near parity to Dubai crude a month ago, traders told Bloomberg on Friday.
Robust crude oil flows out of the Middle East in recent weeks have started to pressure the key metric of strength for physical supply out of the region. The premium of Oman crude over Dubai, the measure of Middle East’s market strength, slumped this week to the lowest level since the end of July.
The Oman-Dubai crude differential had soared to as high as $65 per barrel in March when the Strait of Hormuz was at a virtual closure and no crude cargoes were moving out of the Strait. The premium of Oman crude later slipped into a discount in the three weeks in the middle of June and early July, during which the U.S. and Iran were looking to negotiate a deal.
The differential blew out again in August and especially in September, when hostilities resumed.
But as the Middle Eastern producers accelerated shuttle-shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman, flows have recovered in recent weeks.
The higher availability is depressing the prices of physical crudes from the Middle East in a move that’s opposite to the Brent Crude futures , which jumped to a five-month high of $114 per barrel this week.
The futures market is disconnected from the fundamentals and physical markets as the paper market fears an escalation and renewed supply disruption, while the physical market reflects rising volumes transiting Hormuz.

articles.title_orig: Hacked emails yield revelations on Germany's far-right AfD party leader
articles.title_zh: Hacked emails yield revelations on Germany's far-right AfD party leader
articles.content_orig:
Germany's far-right AfD (Alternative für Deutschland) party has confirmed that it has suffered a security breach, after a hacker published what appear to be hundreds of thousands of the controversial political party's internal emails.
Earlier this week, the AfD admitted that its hosting provider had been hacked in September, and that some of its mailboxes had been copied. The party claims that most of the affected mailboxes had not been used for years, but the leaked archive reportedly includes messages dated as recently as 12 September 2026 .
The news came as the Hexane.cc leak site published AI-written summaries of hundreds of thousands of the messages into categories such as racism and antisemitism, graded Low to Critical, according to local media reports .
To add to the AfD's discomfort, reports suggest that the hacker's access may have been gained in an embarrassingly simple fashion, via a website that had allegedly been left unpatched. However, this has not been independently verified.
What is unusual is that the leaked emails are not published on the site directly. Instead, AI-generated summaries are shown, categorised and rated from Low to Critical. The site encourages anybody who wants to read a complete original email, including headers, message bodies, attachments, and DKIM signatures, to download it via a torrent.
Of course, everyone should be wary of trusting AI-generated summaries, as artificial intelligence has a history of making sometimes large mistakes with great confidence. Indeed, party sources told the media that although the leaked emails appeared to be authentic, the AI-generated summaries appeared to contain several inaccuracies.
The full corpus of 281 GB of stolen messages and files has been made available for download via the torrent, and claims to contain 421,179 stolen internal party emails as well as more than 100,000 files.
The hacker says the leak is intended to expose the party's "degeneracy and hypocrisy."
They have also claimed that someone with a Proton Mail email address reached out to them offering 100,000 Euros if the leak site was taken down.
Should you be tempted to download the torrent and explore the contents of the messages yourself? I would advise against it. In the past, cybercriminals have used torrents of trending topics in the public eye to distribute malware. That's before you even consider the possible legal questions that can arise from handling stolen personal data, whatever you might think of the individuals exposed.
It's not the first cybersecurity headache that the AfD has suffered recently. On 3 September, a press spokesman for the party's group in the Thuringia state parliament warned that his work email account had been used to send phishing emails, and urged recipients not to open PDF attachments they may have received.
Whatever you may think of the AfD, there appear to have been security failures in this case that are far too common. It's not unusual for websites to be overlooked or half-forgotten, and left unpatched. It's not rare for shared infrastructure to not be segmented properly.
Furthermore, whether you are an individual or an organisation, you should be aware that an email account can be a treasure trove of sensitive information. Even if it has not been used for years, it can hold vast amounts of correspondence that can be exploited by hackers and fraudsters.
Graham Cluley is an award-winning security blogger, researcher and public speaker.  He has been working in the computer security industry since the early 1990s.

articles.title_orig: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors
articles.title_zh: US designates helium as a critical material, citing its importance for semiconductors
articles.content_orig:
The United States designated helium as a critical material on Friday, citing its essential role in semiconductor manufacturing and energy production, as well as growing concerns over disruptions to global supplies.
The move by the US Department of Energy will make additional federal funding available to helium producers and bring the material under closer government monitoring.
Helium is mainly extracted as a byproduct of natural gas processing. The US is the world's largest producer of both natural gas and helium, with Qatar and Russia also among the leading helium producers.
Helium exports from Qatar have been severely disrupted by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid its war with Israel and the US. Iranian strikes on Qatari infrastructure have further affected supplies, while Russia introduced temporary export restrictions in April to protect its domestic market.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the Trump administration was seeking to reduce dependence on foreign sources of critical materials, boost domestic manufacturing, support American jobs and strengthen economic and national security.
“President Trump is bringing back America’s manufacturing industry, and that means making sure we have the materials needed to build things in America again,” Wright said in a statement.
While the US is seeking to strengthen domestic production, Europe has faced growing difficulties securing helium supplies, compounded by China's decision in July to impose a temporary export ban on the gas.
Although China is not a major helium producer, it has served as a transit hub for Russian supplies reaching Europe, according to a July report by the Financial Times.
The EU banned direct imports of Russian helium in 2024, but some supplies reportedly continued to reach European markets through China.

articles.title_orig: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.title_zh: King Apple is taking Wall Street’s top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.
Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.
Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.
For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.
Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.
Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.
Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.
Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.
This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .
Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.
Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.
The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

articles.title_orig: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.title_zh: In Troubled Times, Finland’s Public Broadcaster Has an Answer: Puppies
articles.content_orig:
Show features live chat sessions with breeders, a podcast and updates on dogs’ progress from birth to weigh-ins
A 24-hour Finnish TV show dedicated entirely to the live progress of a dog and her six newborn puppies is drawing millions of viewers.
As well as a 24-hour webcam, Pentulive (Puppy Live) includes live evening chat sessions with the dogs’ breeder, a podcast and an instant notification service that updates followers on the puppies’ progress – from their birth to weigh-ins and first nail trims – for eight weeks.
This is the sixth season of the hit show by the broadcaster Yle, and the latest contribution to the growing Nordic cultural phenomenon of “slow TV”.
The trend started in Norway in 2009 with Bergensbanen, a seven-hour train journey broadcast on NRK , and was followed in Sweden by SVT’s Den stora älgvandringen (The Great Moose Migration), which features unnarrated glimpses of moose from the north of the country making their annual journey to summer grazing grounds.
Pentulive has long attracted interest from outside Finland, but this year it is also being broadcast in Sweden (under the name Valparna live ). Yle recently announced that it had also sold the format to a broadcaster in the Netherlands.
Ville Alijoki, the editorial manager of Yle’s factual journalism, said: “There’s a certain magic to it, something that people miss when this world is sometimes quite dark.”
On Saturday, the lagotto romagnolo puppies – four male and two female – will mark their two-week birthday by being officially named after a vote by viewers. Among the nominations are Martha, Timo, Ronja and Dante.
In mid-December, the puppies will leave their mother, Hilkka, and be adopted by new families.
Yle said the current season of Pentulive was on a path to break previous viewing records. Across its first two weeks, the stream has been watched for more than 1m hours, and the show has attracted 1.85 million unique viewers across all related content.
Fans say the puppies offer a relaxing break from work, and comfort from stress, loneliness and illness.
after newsletter promotion
Pirjo Koskinen, a science journalist who came up with the Pentulive concept with the aim of educating viewers on the latest dog research and the importance of the first few weeks of a dog’s life, said the show provided “relief from the terrible things happening in the world”.
She said: “Wars, bombing, climate change, habitat loss etc make us anxious and you can escape, for at least a moment, by watching the canine family.”
Watching the mother and breeder take care of the puppies was like watching “a loop of love and caring”, she said.
“It’s real and we are in the basics of life: the miracle of birth, growth and development. It’s so heartwarming to see eyes opening and first clumsy steps, and it’s happening right now. That brings us joy, but also many funny moments during eight weeks.”

articles.title_orig: The Sigma FP2 brings significant upgrades to the ‘world’s smallest’ full-frame camera
articles.title_zh: The Sigma FP2 brings significant upgrades to the ‘world’s smallest’ full-frame camera
articles.content_orig:
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here's how it works .
Sigma is a company that does things their way, I don't think they think all that much about what others are doing with lens design, and they definitely don't care what others are doing with cameras. They're a lot like Leica, but a lot more affordable. The Sigma BF is definitely its own thing, and the fp2 is too..
These are small companies in the grand scheme of things. It's better to be you than chasing the giants. It's working very well for both of them.
Sigma has announced the FP2, the world's smallest full-frame camera. The camera measures 112.8 x 69.9 x 41.8 mm / 4.4 x 2.8 x 1.6 in and weighs in at 460g with the battery and card. In a full-frame camera, that's quite impressive.
Canon's smallest camera is the EOS R50 V and measures 116 x 85.5 x 68.8 mm / 4.6 x 3.4 x 2.7 in and weighs 370g with the battery. So if you've had an R50 V in your hands, that'll give you an idea of the size.  The big caveat being the APS-C sensor.
The fp2 is almost a complete ground up re-design, a refresh it is not. They have added a 3.15″ tilt screen, and a bigger battery and it's even a bit smaller than its predecessor.
The camera is somehow equipped with two USB-C ports and a full-size HDMI port.
The fp2 is equipped with a partially stacked image sensor, which in turn should lead to faster readout speeds and less rolling shutter. We'll have to wait for the official numbers on that topic, but faster is usually better when it comes to sensors.
If you want to shoot some action stuff, the 20fps is generally more than enough for most people.
Another interesting feature is the 70GB of internal storage. I have a camera with internal storage and it's so annoying that I never use it. Hopefully Sigma has a better implementation.
The camera is no slouch on the video side of things. 6K open gate video, with 12-bit ProRes RAW to SSD. Sigma claims 14.1 stops of dynamic range with L-raw in 4K. You also get dual base ISO settings and 32-bit float audio. That's pretty impressive.
Some consider the FP2 a “modular” camera, as Sigma offers bevy of accessories to fit your needs.
As mentioned, Sigma is also launching a lot of accessories for the fp2. They aren't cheap, but that's probably because this will not be a mass market camera, and it comes down to economies of scale. Hopefully they're well made and do what they do well, especially the EVF and LCD Viewfinder.
5.76M-dot OLED with eye sensor. Connects via a single USB-C port.
OM System / Lumix flash compatible, plus shoe-mount mics and XLR adapters.
Hood-and-loupe viewer that slots onto the rear screen.
Spare Li-ion pack for the fp2. Rated at approx. 370 shots per charge.
External charger for BP-91 batteries.
Bottom plate for mounting and rigging.
I think this looks like a great package for people that may also be looking at a camera like the Panasonic S9, but it seems a lot better for photographers on the surface. The accessory options also add a fair bit to the system.
As far as lenses, there are more out there for you to choose from various brands.
Again, well done Sigma, at least you're definitely not boring.
The Sigma fp2 is the smallest full-frame camera in the world.
Sigma fp2 Click any image to enlarge
Ronkonkoma, N.Y., October 23, 2026
Sigma Corporation of America, the US subsidiary of Sigma Corporation (CEO: Kazuto Yamaki. Headquarters: Asao-ku, Kawasaki-shi, Kanagawa, Japan), is pleased to announce the Sigma FP2 camera, which combines full-fledged shooting capabilities and flexible expandability in the world’s smallest *1 full-frame body. Carrying over the concept of the original fp series while enhancing every function, Sigma has perfected the FP2 as a “Small, Powerful, Adaptable” camera.
Its pocket-sized, lightweight body is equipped with powerful shooting features, from a high-performance full-frame sensor to switching between still and cine modes, each with its own dedicated UI.
The Sigma FP2, a one-of-a-kind compact system camera that offers a high degree of user-oriented adaptability, will be available on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at authorized Sigma retailers starting at $2,199 USD (body only).
The FP2 will also be sold as a bundle with the 50mm F2 DG | Contemporary lens ($2,749) or Electronic Viewfinder EVF-21 ($2,749).
I really like Sigma, but I don’t understand this product. What’s the use of a Body that you can put in your pocket but NOT with an attached lens? I like compact gear but I prefer ergonomic over compact design.
I saw a presentation over the original FP and had hands on it at the “Imaging World“ fair. As I said before: not designed for me. Maybe for others…
There are a lot of pancake lenses for L-mount, so you have that option.
Seems like video shooters prefer this boxy/brick form factor of bodies. Quite a lot of options from almost all camera makers.
The size of the FPII is what I would expect from a R9 camera. The layout might be similar but with a couple of more buttons. Concerning weight, the original is just 1 gr heavier. That kind of gives you a picture of what to expect.
If an R9 goes into that direction, Canon please give it something worth calling a “grip”, at least a hot shoe evf and better ergos in general. I suppose, an LP-E17 would be settled here ﻿ 😔 ﻿
Yeah, the LP-E17 seems to be a Canon favorite… Otoh, Sigmas battery isn’t any better. The only reason the CIPA is better is because there is no EVF. If you compare LCD Cipa ratings, the R8 and R8ii match Sigmas 370 shots :)

articles.title_orig: Etsy to restrict AI-generated content in effort to combat seller slop
articles.title_zh: Etsy to restrict AI-generated content in effort to combat seller slop
articles.content_orig:
Etsy announced new restrictions Thursday on AI-generated content on its platform, saying it threatens the integrity of its sellers’ work and leaves buyers exposed to fraud.
Among the new stipulations:
AI-generated art can still be sold on the platform as long as merchants “Play a clear role in what they create and are transparent about the process,” Etsy said in a note to sellers .
“Our marketplace only works when buyers and sellers trust each other,” Etsy Vice President of Customer Operations James Ossman wrote in a blog post .
“Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it. We know we have work to do to uphold this standard on Etsy.”
Etsy hosts more than 5 million entrepreneurs, most of whom are women who run one-person businesses out of their homes, according to an annual company report.
That distinguishes it from other major e-commerce platforms like Amazon and eBay, though it commands a fraction of those platforms’ revenues. As of 2024, Etsy hosted $10.9 billion-worth of goods’ sales, compared with about $75 billion for eBay and more than $700 billion for Amazon.
Some buyers responded positively to Etsy’s announcement.
“I can’t explain how infuriating it has been to purchase a crochet pattern, only to open the PDF and realize it’s fully AI-generated, doesn’t make sense, and definitely doesn’t match what the finished product should be,” creator Kara Lynne said on X .
The dawn of advanced AI has led to an explosion in AI-generated sales content — and a growing backlash from consumers against what they see as AI slop.
A recent social media trend among cafes and restaurants saw owners pledging not to use AI after egregious examples of AI-generated food images in the wild were shared on social media.
Major platforms are responding to the growing discontent. Many, including Facebook and Instagram, now work to append labels to images or videos created via AI.
Others, like LinkedIn, have added buttons allowing users to report AI-generated content.
Snap has banned wholly AI-generated content from its recommendation algorithm, while Spotify recently announced it had removed 50 million AI-generated tracks from its platform.
Ossman said Etsy would add a function similar to LinkedIn’s that makes it easier for users to report listings that include misleading AI imagery.
He also said Etsy would be using technology to identify misleading imagery and fraudulent listings, with the goal of expanding removals of illicit listings in the coming months.
“We’re actively working to address the questions AI raises for our marketplace,” Ossman said in the post.
“This work is hard, and we don’t have every answer today. But I believe this is an important moment for Etsy, and that these initial steps are putting us on the right path.”
Rob Wile is a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist covering breaking business stories for NBCNews.com.
